# Multi-coin work — current status 15 October 2026

## Active development objective — reaffirmed 15 October 2026

Complete the DEX and integrate the additional coin wallets into the desktop app.
Users retain custody on their own device and can manage wallet keys and recovery
material. Wallet files, seeds, private keys and recovery records must stay on the
user’s system; do not introduce server custody or server storage for that data.
Add authenticated local recovery-key/mnemonic viewing and restoration
with explicit reveal/export consent, compatibility with the wallet's actual
seed derivation, no secret logging or server upload, and tested round-trip recovery.
Do not label an arbitrary encoding of a raw BIP32 seed as a standard BIP39 wallet.

Completion requires accepted desktop create/open/receive/send/backup/restore
flows per supported coin, correct public-chain validation, full light-wallet swap
funding/settlement, interruption and active-trade recovery, peer transport, market
policy and release validation. Research-only markets need a viable verified
protocol before activation. Existing acceptance evidence remains scoped; no
partial wallet or test checkpoint constitutes a complete DEX.


## BCH funding controller and approval checks — passed 15 October 2026

Added separate controller actions for terms, preparation, signing review/approval,
private recovery review/retention, sending, observation, retry and local
acknowledgement. Responses bind to the expected request and operation; approval
expires with the quote and is cleared on new operations/cancellation. Recovery
refreshes the desktop records and requires the final signed identity.

A source-only Claude review informed additional desktop checks: unexpected
review objects are rejected, signing consent must equal the retained commitment,
and completion/start guards block reentrant operations during wallet release.
The fixes were independently checked and tested. Validation passed: 46 targeted
approval checks, the full controller-to-helper actual-node dropped-reply/retry
flow including reentrant callbacks (64 seconds), and the full app build.
Evidence: `build/bch-light-controller-validation-20261015.json`.

Next wire the controller into the authenticated trade session and QML review
screen, then complete BCH/XMZ swap/refund/restart acceptance. The helper bundle
remains unchanged and no public BCH market is enabled.

## BCH desktop helper transport — passed 15 October 2026

Added a BCH-specific desktop process job bound to the selected local wallet,
helper hash, exact configuration and quote bytes. It validates protocol responses,
review commitments, payment identity and endpoint, separates unsigned/signed
transaction IDs, bounds process output and sends passwords only through stdin.
Funding operations hold the selected wallet's exclusive operation lease.

Actual-node tests now pass through Qt into the staged helper: prepare/sign,
private recovery, dropped-reply observation, approved exact-byte retry,
confirmation and local acknowledgement (55.96 seconds). Both raw-seed and BIP39
mnemonic vault signing passed through Qt (32.26 seconds). Tests verify wallet
receive/refresh operations are blocked during funding and the lease is released
afterward. The full app rebuild passed. Evidence:
`build/bch-light-desktop-job-validation-20261015.json`.

Next connect the controller and trading-screen review controls. The tested Qt
probe uses the staged helper; the installed helper bundle is unchanged. No
complete BCH/XMZ swap or Qt process-crash acceptance is claimed here.

## BCH desktop wallet binding and retained context — passed 15 October 2026

The desktop now has a BCH-specific local funding context. Payment intent,
unsigned review and final signed transaction ID are separate immutable records
linked by digests, because BCH signing changes the transaction ID. It rejects
conflicting replacements, orphan/corrupt records and changed configuration, and
stores no seed, password or reusable signing/send approval.

The local wallet funding connection now accepts an explicitly requested BCH coin;
existing Litecoin callers still default to Litecoin. Tests cover coin mismatch,
exclusive wallet operation ownership and source/configuration changes for both.
Validation passed: 54 context checks, 61 desktop tests with 21 fixture-dependent
skips, and a full app rebuild. Evidence:
`build/bch-light-desktop-context-validation-20261015.json`.

Next connect the BCH helper process/response validation and review controls to
this context and the selected wallet. No BCH trading UI is enabled yet; the
bundled helper remains at its earlier tested version pending integration.

## BCH helper interrupted-send recovery — passed 15 October 2026

The staged helper now supports retry review, separately approved retry and local
acknowledgement reconciliation. Retry reopens the exact signed claim, validates
the original trade intent/endpoint and current quote, and uses a fresh chain
observation. Included transactions and missing prior intents cannot be retried.
Acknowledgement reconciliation uses saved receipts without network requests and
does not treat chain inclusion as a send acknowledgement.

Two actual BCH Node scenarios passed: server reply dropped after acceptance
(49.33 seconds), and the owned helper killed with SIGKILL after acceptance
(49.47 seconds). New helper processes recovered the uncertain outcome, rejected
ordinary resend and stale approval, retried identical signed bytes with fresh
approval, observed confirmation and recovered the trade acknowledgement/peer
funding message. Compilation, release builds and patch audit passed. Evidence:
`build/bch-light-helper-retry-validation-20261015.json`.

Next: desktop BCH funding/recovery integration and complete BCH/XMZ settlement,
refund and restart acceptance. These tests do not cover power loss, key-only
active-trade recovery, public chains or a complete swap. The desktop bundle
remains unchanged.

## Lost broadcast acknowledgement and restart — 13 October 2026

The owned Electrum fixture now drops one TLS reply **after the LTC node accepts

response, and does not automatically retry. After process restart and saved
recovery exchange, observation finds the transaction pending while the local
broadcast acknowledgement remains unknown. A fresh retry review/approval sends

broadcast attempts (original plus explicit retry), then confirms the transaction.

The complete resumed trade also passes both-chain cancellation/refunds, exact
local LTC balance, XMZ refund payout, reorganization checks and final app reopening.
**92 QML tests passed**, including uncertain-outcome presentation and disabled

Evidence: `build/light-lost-ack-restart-20261013.json` and
`build/light-lost-ack-validation-20261013.json`. All owned processes completed and

## Active trade restart after LTC broadcast — 13 October 2026

Added a production **Resume saved recovery exchange** action, separate from
reopening a funding reservation. The native session reads the retained recovery
PSBT from a private bounded record; the existing recovery helper validates it
against the committed checkpoint before requesting any identity signature. It
never reserves new wallet inputs or requires fresh funding terms. Missing or
malformed records fail closed. The UI exposes this action when a saved local
payment needs peer recovery again.

Accepted owned-chain test: kill the idle app process after acknowledged local LTC
broadcast but before confirmation, restart from the same journals/preferences,
reconnect both peers, restore the remembered wallet and identical payment/review/
transaction, reject a malformed recovery record and old send consent, resume peer
recovery, observe the pending transaction and explicitly retry its exact bytes.
The restarted app then completes XMZ funding and both-chain cancellation/refunds,
including exact local LTC balance, reorganization rejection and final app reopening.

**60 native tests and 91 QML tests passed**, plus full app build and helper bundle
checks. Evidence: `build/light-active-restart-20261013.json` and
`build/light-active-restart-validation-20261013.json`. All owned runs are terminal.

Scope is one acknowledged-broadcast, idle-operation interruption boundary. It does
not prove interruption during signing, a lost broadcast acknowledgement, filesystem
power loss, or recovery from keys alone. Those boundaries and public/light settlement
remain required; public market gates stay closed.

## Production local refund-address guard — 13 October 2026

The local LTC funding helper now verifies that the negotiated refund address
belongs to an allocation retained by the selected wallet. It checks public account
and network identity, includes explicitly retained recovery/discovery coverage,
limits lookup to the validated address journal's 10,000-entry maximum, and rechecks
saved bytes. Terms, preparation, signature review/signing and initial send review/send
all apply the check before chain synchronization or funding mutation. The helper
never silently allocates a new refund address or changes an approved quote.
Observation and exact retry of retained transactions keep their existing recovery
checks without adding this fresh-address gate. Signing still authenticates the vault.
The trade panel explains that a different refund address requires a new quote.

Accepted: **201 wallet tests passed**, **3 DEX command tests passed**, **90 QML
tests passed**; all-feature/all-target checks, patch reconstruction, full app build
and helper packaging passed. Actual controller funding passed for raw-seed and
BIP39 wallets. Both formats reject unrelated refund addresses with no wallet-file
mutation or network query. The complete app-peer refund path also passed with the
new guard, including local LTC balance, XMZ refund, reorganization handling and
app-state reopening.

Evidence: `build/light-refund-ownership-{acceptance,paired,bundle,validation}-20261013.json`.
Current bundled helper: `build/light-refund-ownership-helper-tested-20261013`, SHA256
`ab6fbb7efa41cf7d07949b20ae9d06c82b5a68887a27452dee22c6c204010631`.
This supersedes the production ownership gap listed in the preceding checkpoint.
Next: interrupt and resume an active locally funded trade across process restarts;
then complete public-network/light settlement and remaining coin integrations.
Public market gates remain closed.

confirmed XMZ payout. Both live Qt peers perform startup, recovery agreement and
redemption exchange. The LTC BIP39 wallet signs locally, requires separate signing
and send approvals, rejects reused/wrong-action consent, broadcasts through the
owned TLS Electrum peer, retries the identical transaction, and verifies inclusion.
The existing app settlement flow then confirms XMZ funding, redeems LTC, restores
and reopens the local XMZ claim wallet, prepares/sends the payout, and checks exact
recipient balances and reserve return. Confirmation checks reject reorganized
chain evidence and accept freshly confirmed evidence. Funding fees are computed
from transaction inputs/outputs without assuming ownership by the Core wallet.

**Accepted:** `build/light-app-settlement-20261013.json`; native Qt regression
**60 passed, 0 failed, 21 fixture-dependent skips**. Full test process and owned
nodes exited. Reproduction: `build/run-light-app-settlement-20261013.py` (use new
report/log names for another run). Provenance:
`build/light-app-settlement-validation-20261013.json`.

Scope: local LTC funding integrated with the existing **node-backed** private
settlement services on regtest/fakechain. This is not proof of a fully light,
public-network DEX. Cancellation/refund into a user-controlled local wallet,
interrupted active-trade restart/recovery, public-chain settlement observation,
and the other coin swap integrations remain required. Public market gates stay
closed. The earlier recovery-only checkpoint remains valid but is superseded for
the success path by this complete paired-chain acceptance.

## Active desktop wallet binding and funding interlock — 13 October 2026

An in-process interlock prevents normal wallet operations during a funding command;
wallet availability reflects it through `busy` and `dexFundingBusy`. Completion,
failed commands and cancellation release the interlock. Engine storage leases
remain responsible for cross-process protection and durable input reservations.

## Desktop activation and guarded reopening — 13 October 2026

The desktop now offers separately approved activation after a fresh recovery
backup verification. It requires the exact recovery digest and another local
password entry, then validates the helper activation response against retained
intent/completion records and the active configuration derived from the pending
configuration. The source account, storage paths and endpoint cannot change.
Passwords clear after submission, context/view changes, inactivity and timeout.

or contacting a server, but only with matching activation intent, completion,
recovery/context commitments and exact active configuration bytes. An active file
without completion remains pending as `wallet-import-activation-incomplete`;
modified/conflicting records produce `wallet-import-activation-invalid` with
wallet controls disabled. Historical activation does not restore a current
backup-verification claim. Later legitimate address allocation does not invalidate

## Authenticated recovery and backup coordination — 13 October 2026

The engine now combines password authentication, durable address allocation
retention and exact encrypted backup verification. A private context binds the
independently approved configuration/coverage commitments, account, encrypted
vault digest and backup directory. A fresh operation rejects a destination
already containing a backup before changing addresses. Completion is retained
only after read-back verification of the current vault and allocation snapshot.

Every retry authenticates again and rechecks the backup; historical completion
is not fresh verification. Allocation and backup publication can resume from
retained records without replacing ciphertext. If interruption occurs before
an allocation intent exists, the caller must obtain a fresh matching discovery
review and use the begin operation again. Backup context alone cannot invent
scan coverage. A changed vault, destination or approval cannot be silently adopted.

This coordinator is still an engine API, not yet a desktop recovery control.
Its receipt explicitly leaves activation false, complete history unproven and
active-trade recovery unsupported. Next: private helper request/response wiring,
restart-aware GUI recovery controls and separately approved activation. Packaged
helper/GUI binaries and mining settings are unchanged.

## Exact recovery-backup verification — 13 October 2026

Mnemonic backup verification now binds the encrypted backup to the exact current
vault ciphertext and address allocation record, including reservation identities.
A valid password or matching address counts alone cannot make an older or
conflicting backup current. `retain_current` authenticates first, retains a
snapshot in a separate caller-selected private directory, reads it back and
reuses identical ciphertext on retry. It never replaces the initial backup.

This is a recovery coordination prerequisite. It does not retain discovery
allocations, publish a recovery journal, activate imported wallets, certify
complete history or recover active trades. The helper and GUI do not call these
new engine APIs yet; their packaged binaries have not changed in this checkpoint.

## Reviewed recovery allocation coverage — 13 October 2026

A successful two-branch wallet observation can now produce an opaque recovery
coverage review. The review binds the public account, selected chain height/tip,
existing allocation digest, known prior allocation counts, scan floor/gap and
proposed branch counts. It cannot be created from deserialized caller claims.
Both branches must have covered existing/known allocations before reaching
their reported gaps; insufficient bounds fail instead of producing a complete
wallet claim.

After exact approval, the engine can conservatively retain **all scanned
indices**, including addresses reported empty, through the existing atomic
address-book update. Existing request identities survive; the next fresh
receiving/change allocation begins after the scanned range. A reopened book
already at the target counts needs no rewrite; other allocation changes require
new review. Account and selected-chain mismatches are refused. This only avoids
reuse inside the reviewed range: server omissions and use beyond it remain
possible. The review explicitly says history completeness is unproven and a
new encrypted backup is required.

The setup engine can now accept an existing English BIP39 mnemonic and optional

select coin/network/account index and fresh private directories. Import has a
separate retained setup mode: it cannot adopt a generated-wallet setup or be

before the intent is retained; matching retries reuse the ciphertext and reject
a changed phrase, passphrase, password or account context.

wallet schemas and persisted context bytes remain compatible.

## Bundled Linux light-wallet helper — 13 October 2026

Linux prototype builds can now bundle the reviewed `native-ltc-light` helper.
The builder supplies both `MONZERO_LIGHT_HELPER` (absolute binary path) and
`MONZERO_LIGHT_HELPER_SHA256` (expected lowercase digest). Configuration rejects
missing/mismatched pins or bundling without the Linux prototype build. The
expected digest is compiled into the GUI, not loaded from an adjacent manifest.
The helper is copied to `bin/monzero-light/native-ltc-light` and installed by the
`LightWalletHelper` component with mode 0555; copying avoids source hardlinks.

With prototype opt-in, the GUI uses that bundled helper automatically unless
explicit helper startup arguments are supplied. Runtime verification still
checks the executable and expected digest. Missing/modified bundles fail startup;
without opt-in the bundled helper is not activated. No wallet secrets are part
of the package. Signed release distribution, non-Linux provisioning and reviewed
migration of existing launcher helper paths/digests remain separate unfinished
work. Old saved launchers are not silently rewritten to accept a new helper.

Acceptance: configured and built the real desktop against the already-tested
helper (`../build/light-wallet-bundle-configure-20261013.log`,
`../build/light-wallet-bundle-build-20261013.log`).
`../build/light-wallet-bundle-20261013.json` records standalone CMake rejection
checks, installed digest/mode verification and four full-GUI namespace cases:
opt-out without helper, valid opt-in bundle, missing bundle and modified bundle.
The GUI tests hide the host home and disable network access. This verifies
packaging/startup, not funded wallet operation or DEX settlement.

## Remembered local wallet folders — 13 October 2026

Guided creation and explicit folder reopening now remember one wallet folder

When the separately trusted setup helper is enabled at startup, unconfigured
coins attach their remembered settings after verifying the same helper path
and digest. Explicit startup wallet selections take precedence.

Automatic attachment leaves keys locked and makes no helper or network request.

## Missing-vault recovery implementation — 13 October 2026

Added raw-seed restoration in the wallet engine and local helper. It targets the
account already saved in the user's private configuration, verifies that the
seed derives that exact public account, and encrypts a missing vault with the
provided password. Existing vault ciphertext is never replaced; an identical
retry must authenticate and retain the same bytes. Configuration-digest approval,
chain identity and an explicit seed-format tag are required at the helper boundary.
The request carries secrets only over local stdin, never command-line arguments.

The desktop now exposes this operation in the shared local recovery panel for
LTC/BTC/BCH/DOGE. It requires a lowercase raw seed, matching new passwords and
explicit approval, clears entered material on submission or view/coin changes,
and validates the helper acknowledgement against the selected account, chain,
wallet and request. Secrets are sent over helper stdin and excluded from the
public status map. This does not recover a lost configuration.
Address allocations and trade journals remain untouched; full seed-only recovery
will need discovery and allocation handling before ordinary receiving/spending is
safe. Mnemonic wallet support remains a separate unfinished compatibility task.

## Mnemonic format development — 13 October 2026

Added explicit BIP39 material handling through pinned `bip39` 2.2.0 with its
zeroize feature: 24-word OS-random generation, checksum-validated English import
(12/15/18/21/24 words), optional NFKD-normalized passphrase derivation, and the
full standard 64-byte seed. No legacy raw seed is relabelled as a mnemonic.

A new `MZMNEM01` encrypted record stores mnemonic entropy and the optional
BIP39 passphrase, protected by the local vault password. These two passwords
have different purposes. The record uses the existing private journal,
XChaCha20-Poly1305 and fixed scrypt cost, binding chain and wallet identity in
its authenticated header. It retains the existing vault filename to prevent
one format shadowing another; existing raw-vault readers reject this version.

This is engine groundwork, not an activated desktop mnemonic wallet. Creation
selection, helper/private reveal, signing, versioned backups and restoration
must be integrated before offering this format to users. Existing desktop
wallet creation still uses the accepted raw-seed format. Current installed
helper acceptance does not prove mnemonic operation.

Reference: [BIP39](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki)
and [bip39 2.2.0](https://docs.rs/bip39/2.2.0/bip39/struct.Mnemonic.html).
Public test vectors from Trezor are retained with a source download hash.
Patch `upstream-light-wallet-mnemonic-core.patch` reconstructs the source and
lockfile; only three new dependency versions were added, with existing package
versions preserved. Audit: `../build/light-mnemonic-patch-audit-20261013.log`.
The focused derivation tests passed, including all 24 published English vectors,
NFKD passphrase equivalence, checksum rejection and four-chain account recovery:
`../build/light-mnemonic-tests-20261013.log`.
Final all-features/all-targets compile passed:
`../build/light-mnemonic-final-all-targets-20261013.log`.
Full wallet suite: 183 passed, seven ignored, including encrypted mnemonic
reopen across four coins and refusal to overwrite a mnemonic vault with a legacy
vault: `../build/light-mnemonic-wallet-suite-20261013.log`.

## Mnemonic encrypted backup implementation — 13 October 2026

Added versioned `MZMNBK01` bundles containing the encrypted mnemonic vault and
address allocation record. Export authenticates the password and account before
encrypting the bundle; inspect/load/save authenticate chain and wallet identity,
phrase/passphrase derivation and allocation-record binding. Backups use the
existing private journal and never replace a different backup generation.

Restore preflights both retained records before writing either. An interruption
after vault publication can be retried with the identical bundle; a conflicting
address record prevents the vault write. Restoring over newer allocations is
refused rather than rolling the address history back. As with legacy backups,
this excludes active trades and cannot establish backup freshness on an empty
machine; chain discovery and trade journals remain separate responsibilities.

This is engine backup support. Helper dispatch and desktop mnemonic workflows
remain unfinished. Existing raw-wallet backup formats and operations remain in
place, and these bundles do not activate mnemonic wallets in the desktop.

Source: `upstream-light-wallet-mnemonic-backup.patch`.
All-features/all-targets compile and ordered patch reconstruction passed:
`../build/light-mnemonic-backup-all-targets-20261013.log` and
`../build/light-mnemonic-backup-patch-audit-20261013.log`.
Full wallet suite: 186 passed, seven ignored,
`../build/light-mnemonic-backup-wallet-suite-20261013.log`.
The four-chain backup matrix preserves phrase, passphrase, account and receive/
change allocations through encrypted save/load and interrupted restore; exact
retries retain unchanged bytes. Wrong passwords/chain/wallet, ciphertext

## Local-custody continuation — 13 October 2026

The desktop application owns generated wallets. Seeds, private keys, passwords,
wallet files and backups must not be uploaded to a Monzero custody service.
Local seed vaults and backups are encrypted; address records and chain caches
are local data, not necessarily encrypted. Network access still queries chain
servers and relays approved signed transactions. External servers may observe
query metadata; local custody is not a promise of zero network disclosure.

Claude's 12 October shared LTC/BTC/BCH/DOGE helper changes are present. The
handoff and recorded four-chain payment acceptance were reviewed. A new check
now passes creation, repeat creation without replacing the wallet, backup
verification, wrong-password rejection, wrong-chain rejection, restoration and
matching first receive addresses for all four coins with networking disabled.
Bubblewrap makes the filesystem read-only except for disposable local folders;
all generated directories/files are checked for owner-only 0700/0600 permissions.
No user wallet, node, mining process or live funds were used.

Evidence: [local-custody acceptance](../build/light-wallet-local-custody-20261013.json).
This does not establish mainnet readiness, online-query privacy, secure memory,
full trade recovery or multi-coin desktop integration. A custody/backup explanation
has been added to the existing Litecoin desktop panel. Its presentation suite
passes 70 tests (0 failures, 0 skips); log:
[QML custody regression](../build/light-wallet-custody-qml-20261013.log).

Next implementation sequence:

1. Generalize desktop helper configuration, request/response validation and
   address handling for explicit LTC/BTC/BCH/DOGE identities. Preserve existing
   LTC persisted formats and isolate wallet records by coin, network and wallet.
   Verify mismatched configurations/responses fail before enabling new panels.
2. Connect coin selection to local create/open/receive/backup/restore controls,
   with explicit review of storage paths and public-server choice. Keep BCH/DOGE
   restricted to regtest until their header validation is implemented.
3. Implement pinned BCH checkpoint/ASERT validation, then DOGE DigiShield/AuxPoW
   and checkpoint validation. BTC testnet4 remains a separate unsupported target.
4. Integrate light-wallet funding into swaps, retaining separate signing and
   broadcast approvals, uncertain-send recovery and active-trade backups.
5. Repeat actual-node desktop acceptance per coin before any activation decision.


## Revised delivery estimates — 11 October 2026

The earlier 4–8-week GUI / 8–16-week public-pilot estimates are superseded.
They described an earlier BTC/XMZ scope and understated the expanded project.
There is no agreed capacity/start-date baseline to quantify exact schedule slippage.
These replacements are provisional engineering judgement, not velocity-based forecasts.
Assume one continuous full-time workstream of roughly 30–40 focused hours per week,
LTC/BCH first, prompt decisions, no new scope, and routine integration/retest effort.
External reviewer waits and major protocol redesign are additional.
Confidence is low; half the assumed capacity could roughly double elapsed time.

## Litecoin contract milestone

`tools/dex-engine-port/upstream-litecoin-contract-fixture.patch` adds an isolated
Rust integration test to the pinned engine. The ordered patch verifier includes
it after the existing local or CachyOS patch series. The later script-constructor patch described below updates shared transaction
construction while preserving the existing Bitcoin address API. Network adapters
remain unchanged.

The Python driver `tools/dex-engine-port/test_litecoin_settlement.py` owns a
private Litecoin regtest node with no external peers and a disposable wallet.
It uses actual engine transaction constructors and deterministic public test
keys. It checks exact lock value and destination scripts, redeem adaptor
recovery, refund adaptor recovery of the shared native spend key, rejection
before the relative timelock boundary, acceptance at the boundary, exact
confirmed witness bytes and payouts, node restart and reorg/reconfirmation.
Invalid amounts, excessive fees, invalid timelocks and unsupported scripts are
rejected before funding. Four Rust tests also exercise malformed requests and
funding PSBTs. Private fixture results are created exclusively with mode 0600.

This is not a negotiated two-party LTC/XMZ swap: no native wallet is funded by
this fixture, and it does not test DLEQ negotiation, trade-process crash recovery,
ambiguous submission or fee changes. The initial fixture used Bitcoin `Address` internally as a script carrier. The
script-constructor milestone removes that dependency from the Litecoin path.
The Litecoin node independently derives and validates the `rltc` lock address.

The tested daemon is official Litecoin Core 0.21.5.8 x86_64 Linux, archive SHA256
`43200c9f9d65ebc126ea5833ca9429e144c4b3273da6bb9f4e89fd7450ab1be9`.
Regtest genesis is pinned in the Python driver. CSV is active. MWEB activation
is deliberately postponed with `-vbparams=mweb:0:0:1000000:2000000`, verified
by RPC: default MWEB activation caused mining failure at height 431 in this
fixture. Results therefore cover transparent contracts only, not MWEB coexistence.

Run after applying/verifying the ordered engine patches and building the test:

```sh
# In the pinned engine, with the configured Rust toolchain:
cargo test -p swap-core --test litecoin_settlement --locked
# In monzero-gui; select the exact compiled integration test executable:
python3 -u tools/dex-engine-port/test_litecoin_settlement.py \
  --litecoind /absolute/path/to/litecoind \
  --engine-test-binary /absolute/path/to/litecoin_settlement-TEST_HASH \
  --temp-parent ../build \
  --report build/litecoin-contract-results-UNIQUE.json
```

The report path must not already exist. Fixture data is removed and the owned
node stopped on completion or failure. CachyOS logs and results are in
`build/litecoin-refund-compile.log`, `build/litecoin-refund-contract-test.log`
and `build/litecoin-refund-contract-results.json`. The same real-chain fixture
also passed locally. Both machines passed `swap-core --all-features --all-targets`:
79 library tests plus four fixture tests, with the explicitly invoked chain
exporter ignored in normal test runs. Ordered patch reconstruction passed on
both machines. The daemon archive checksum was verified before local extraction.

## Approved routed-trade design

The user explicitly approved sequential routed trades on 2026-09-25. A route
such as XMZ → BTC → XMR consists of separate swaps. Each leg must show its own
provider, fees, destination, expiry, minimum proceeds, approval and recovery.
Completion of the first leg can leave the user holding BTC if the next leg is
unavailable; the whole route is not atomic. Approval of one leg must never
start or fund another. Native RUNE must not silently become an ERC-20 token.

The architecture audit found two prerequisites: the native GUI currently saves
a quote reservation but has no production negotiation/execution driver, and
the upstream BTC/XMR start operation depends on its desktop maker-selection
flow. Its CLI resume/refund commands do not provide a headless start operation.
Simply dispatching the existing test flow or marking a registry entry executable
would not implement a route.

Implementation order: finish the native driver and durable execution claim;
connect explicit GUI execution approval; persist route and per-leg ownership
and recovery state; integrate a reviewed second-leg start API and independently
validated quotes. No external route provider is currently enabled, and no route
can broadcast. Route recovery must reconcile uncertain submissions before
retrying and retain the independently owned intermediate payout.

## Transparent destination-script integration

`upstream-transparent-script-spends.patch` adds
`TxLock::build_spend_transaction_to_script`,
`TxCancel::build_spend_transaction_to_script`, `TxRedeem::new_to_script` and
`TxFullRefund::new_to_script`. Existing Bitcoin-address APIs delegate to these
constructors, preserving their public signatures and transaction behavior.
The Litecoin fixture now passes destination scripts directly without creating
Bitcoin address objects. These low-level APIs do not validate a chain or fee
policy; callers retain that responsibility. They do not make DOGE or BCH
compatible with Bitcoin SegWit contracts.

A compatibility test compares legacy and script constructors across P2WPKH,
P2WSH and P2TR destinations: spend transactions, redeem/refund transaction IDs,
signature hashes, observer scripts and completed signed transactions. Both
machines passed 79 core library tests plus five fixture tests. The ignored
exporter is invoked by the real-chain harness. Both machines passed the
Litecoin harness again using these constructors, including adaptor recovery,
relative-lock rejection/acceptance, exact payouts, node restart and reorg.
Logs: `build/litecoin-script-core-tests.log` and
`build/litecoin-script-contract-test.log`. The ordered patch verifier preserves
each machine's existing patch series and appends the two Litecoin patches.

Local Claude's read-only review found no blocking regression in this patch.
It identified remaining Litecoin work: punishment and early-refund constructors
still take Bitcoin addresses, other optional recovery paths are not ported,
and static fee-weight helpers assume a P2WPKH destination. The fixture uses an
explicit atomic fee and records actual vsize; production fee policy must use
the actual destination weight. Low-level constructors also retain existing
caller preconditions against fee underflow and dust. This review is not a
security audit. Its output is `build/litecoin-script-claude-review.log`.

The next contract milestone must include punishment after cancellation when
the refund party stops responding, plus early refund, before treating the
Litecoin recovery graph as covered. Neither script APIs nor the current chain
fixtures supply a Litecoin wallet adapter or versioned LTC/XMZ negotiation.

The local swap-machine build passed with all features and targets enabled,
including rebuilt BTC settlement integration tests. Its library suite passed
91 tests (two integration-only cases ignored). The rebuilt BTC/XMZ redemption
fixture also passed with `--native-spendable`, including exact-net relay,
dropped-reply reconciliation, wallet reopen and top-up/claim mechanics.
Log: `build/litecoin-script-btc-redeem.log`. These findings retain the limits
on protocol fee enforcement and production key storage described above.

The matching rebuilt BTC/XMZ cancellation/full-refund fixture also passed
with `--native-spendable`; see `build/litecoin-script-btc-refund.log`. Both
regressions completed successfully and stopped their owned fixture processes.

## Early refund and punishment contract milestone

`upstream-litecoin-recovery-paths.patch` adds script-based constructors for
`TxEarlyRefund` and `TxPunish`, retaining the existing Bitcoin-address API as
a delegating wrapper. The transaction version, signature digest, input
sequence, destination observer and fee subtraction remain unchanged. The
constructor compatibility test now compares signed bytes for these paths too.

The fixture request and result schemas are now v2; `punishBlocks` is mandatory
and bounded to 1–65535, independently of `cancelBlocks`. Punishment pays the
redeem destination after cancellation; early refund pays the refund destination
directly from the original lock. The Rust exporter verifies outpoints, exact
amounts, scripts and punishment sequence before returning transactions.

The actual Litecoin harness passed on both machines for redemption, full refund,
early refund and punishment. It tests the punishment transaction at one
confirmation and one block before maturity (both rejected), then accepts it at
the boundary. Early refund succeeds before cancellation matures. Each path
checks exact confirmed witness bytes and payout, node restart, loss of
confirmation on reorg, reconfirmation and rejection of competing spends after
confirmation. A fresh lock funds each scenario. Both machines passed the core
suite (79 library tests and five fixture tests), and the final expanded BTC
constructor compatibility test passed locally. Ordered patch reconstruction
passed on both machines.

Logs: `build/litecoin-recovery-core-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-recovery-contract-test.log`; public results are in
`build/litecoin-recovery-contract-results.json`. These remain transparent-chain
fixtures with MWEB postponed. They do not negotiate with a remote party, prove
pre-signature exchange, fund XMZ, authorize a production early refund, or test
the optional partial-refund/reclaim/mercy protocol. A production driver must
restrict early refund to its negotiated protocol state.

The local swap-machine all-features/all-targets build and 91 library tests
passed after this patch. The rebuilt BTC/XMZ cancellation/full-refund fixture
passed with native spending and recovery checks; log:
`build/litecoin-recovery-btc-refund.log`.

Claude's read-only review found no blocking code issue, but identified that
rejection of a competing transaction could be caused by immaturity and that
the one-block reorg did not remove cancellation itself. The harness now requires
Litecoin Core's exact `missing-inputs` rejection after a competing confirmed
spend, including early refund after cancellation. It also invalidates the
cancellation block on the punishment path, re-mines cancellation, checks
punishment is again non-final at one confirmation and one block before maturity,
then verifies the original punishment confirms at the new boundary. The first
strict rejection run expected a newer Bitcoin error name and failed; Litecoin
0.21.5.8 reports `missing-inputs`. The corrected stronger runs passed locally and on CachyOS;
log: `build/litecoin-recovery-reorg-test.log`.

Network parameters for the upcoming Litecoin address adapter were checked
against [Litecoin Core 0.21.5.8 chain parameters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/litecoin-project/litecoin/v0.21.5.8/src/chainparams.cpp).
This milestone does not yet add that adapter or activate any market.

## Litecoin address and deployment boundary

`upstream-litecoin-addresses.patch` adds `LtcNetwork` and `LtcSegwitAddress` to
swap-core. Mainnet, testnet and regtest have separate Litecoin HRPs and pinned
genesis hashes from the official 0.21.5.8 chain parameters linked above. Chain
name and genesis must both match the configured network. The address type
retains its network, canonical encoding and destination script privately;
there is no conversion through a Bitcoin address or unchecked deserialization.

Supported destinations are native P2WPKH, P2WSH and P2TR. The boundary rejects
wrong-network/BTC prefixes, invalid checksums, noncanonical case or whitespace,
oversized input, MWEB, legacy addresses and unsupported witness programs.
Canonical lowercase is required. Encoding a P2TR destination is not evidence
of Taproot activation or wallet ownership; a wallet driver must separately
verify its deployment policy and actual node. Likewise a node-supplied genesis
claim does not authenticate that node.

The fixture schema is now v3. It requires observed chain identity plus both
Litecoin destination addresses and their expected scripts. It verifies those
bindings before transaction construction. The Python harness compares the
engine-generated P2WSH lock address to Litecoin Core's independently decoded
address and uses node-generated P2WPKH destination addresses for all four
settlement/recovery paths. Wrong chain, wrong genesis and destination mismatch
are rejected before funding.

Both machines passed the core all-features/all-targets suite: 81 library tests
and five fixture tests, with the chain exporter intentionally ignored in normal
runs. Both real-chain runs passed all four paths with address validation,
exact payouts, restart, competing-input rejection and cancellation re-anchoring.
Logs: `build/litecoin-address-core-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-address-contract-test.log`; results:
`build/litecoin-address-contract-results.json`.

The first full run exposed a pre-existing randomized Bitcoin fee test that
unconditionally expected success for a generated dust amount of one atom.
The estimator intentionally rejects amounts at or below its dust threshold.
The property now asserts rejection for that range and retains its fee-ceiling
assertion for accepted amounts. The failing seed is retained for replay. Fee
estimator production behavior was not changed. An initial test import used a
private module path; it was corrected to the public constant re-export before
the passing builds. Ordered source reconstruction passes on both machines.

The production Litecoin wallet/observer, versioned LTC/XMZ quote negotiation,
route driver and GUI execution wiring remain unfinished; no market was enabled.

Claude's read-only address review found no blocking issue. In response to its
reviewability finding, the unrelated dust-property repair and replay seed were
separated into `upstream-fee-dust-property.patch`; the Litecoin address patch
contains only its module/export and fixture integration. Both ordered patch
verifiers pass after the split. Review log: `build/litecoin-address-claude-review.log`.
This remains development review, not a security audit.

## Litecoin wallet RPC preparation and observation

`upstream-litecoin-wallet-rpc.patch` introduces a loopback-only authenticated
`LitecoinRpc` adapter in swap-machine. It prepares unsigned lock PSBTs and reads
current unspent outputs. It has no signing, broadcasting or automatic retry API.
The configured wallet name is restricted to an unambiguous endpoint component;
credentials are retained in zeroizing buffers with no Debug/serialization API.
The HTTP client disables proxies and redirects, bounds response bodies, uses
request identities and timeouts, and rejects node errors and HTTP failures.

Before and after funding preparation, it checks Litecoin chain/genesis, CSV and
SegWit activation, synchronization, the expected wallet name/private-key state,
and an owned anchor address/script. Change is generated by that wallet and
independently checked for ownership. Exact decimal strings avoid floating-point
principal and fee conversion. Returned PSBTs must have a single exact shared
principal output and at most one owned change output, native SegWit funding
inputs, no duplicate inputs or signatures, consistent UTXO metadata, and a fee
matching both the PSBT accounting and the caller's fee ceiling.

UTXO observations bind the response to an unchanged chain tip and expose the
exact amount, script and confirmation count. The view excludes mempool transactions. Absence means confirmed-chain
unspent-output absence; it does not prove never-funded, redeemed or refunded.
This adapter trusts the caller-owned local Core service; an unauthenticated
network observation or a caller-supplied genesis string is not sufficient.

The Litecoin harness accepts `--wallet-test-binary` pointing to the new
`litecoin_wallet_rpc-*` exporter. When supplied, all four paths use the Rust
adapter's unsigned PSBT, verify preparation does not change balances, the
mempool or locked coins, reject wrong-wallet/foreign-anchor/insufficient-fee
requests, and check funded and spent lock observations. The first run failed
because the test sent an outpoint as a JSON object; the Rust library expects
its canonical `txid:vout` string. Correcting that harness format produced a
passing full local chain run. Result files explicitly record whether the wallet
adapter was exercised. Run logs: `build/litecoin-wallet-contract-test.log`.

Local swap-machine tests passed 94 cases (two integration-only cases ignored),
including PSBT mutation rejection and bounded mocked HTTP responses. The test
exporter remains ignored unless explicitly driven with an owned regtest cookie.
No wallet session secrets or funded PSBTs are written to public logs.

**Still required:** durable input ownership and reservation recovery, transaction
signing tied to negotiated terms, ambiguous-broadcast reconciliation, LTC/XMZ
peer negotiation and GUI execution. An unsigned preview deliberately does not
reserve inputs; it must never be used as a durable funding authorization. The
existing market activation gate remains unchanged.

The real-node harness verifies the lock remains visible during an unconfirmed

Funding previews explicitly disable opt-in RBF and validate version 2, zero

## Litecoin durable funding reservations

`litecoin_rpc::reservation` now records an immutable trade preparation before
locking wallet coins. The record binds the trade UUID, Litecoin genesis, wallet
anchor, contract/change addresses, exact PSBT, principal and fee ceiling.
Input claims use chain/outpoint identities shared across wallets and trades.
A canonical private directory and a nonblocking directory flock serialize all
reservations using that journal. Linux publication uses a synced temporary file
and `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` followed by directory fsync; interrupted temp
files never become claims. Existing records must match exactly.

Before input claims are written, every claim is checked for conflicts and every
input is checked against a stable confirmed-chain view, wallet ownership, PSBT
amount/script metadata, and the mempool UTXO view. Core coin locks are restored
idempotently from the original intent after restart. A resume cannot choose new
inputs or reprice the transaction. Spent inputs fail and require reconciliation;
this API does not identify whether the spending transaction was ours.

The isolated harness exercises reserve/reopen/restart for each settlement branch,
checks an independently populated second trade cannot claim the same inputs,
rejects changed preparation and wrong-wallet requests, and rejects resume after
the lock spends those inputs both before and after confirmation. Unit checks
cover journal exclusivity, immutable records, orphan temporary files, unsafe
permissions, symlinks and hardlinks. Claude reviewed the first implementation;
atomic publication and all-input preflight address its concrete write/interleaved
claim issues. Remaining startup inventory and reconciliation concerns remain open.

**Not execution authority:** this is one-trade preparation and recovery. A future
wallet coordinator must restore all pending reservations before offering new
funding previews, maintain exclusive wallet control, bind signing to negotiated
commercial terms and recovery transactions, and reconcile ambiguous broadcasts.
No automatic unlock/release or signing/broadcast API is exposed here. Using
multiple journal directories for the same wallet breaks reservation exclusivity
and is outside the caller contract. Mainnet/MWEB remains unverified.

Validation for the corrected reservation implementation passed on both machines:
95 local and 98 CachyOS library tests, with 2 explicit external fixtures ignored;
all-feature/all-target package builds; all four real Litecoin settlement branches
with reservation restart/rejection checks; and ordered engine patch verification.
Evidence: `build/litecoin-reservation-build.log`,
`build/litecoin-reservation-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-reservation-reviewed-chain.log`, and
`build/litecoin-reservation-reviewed-results.json` on each machine.
The additional three CachyOS unit tests belong to its preserved patch78 changes.


## Litecoin exact funding reconciliation

`observe_lock` reads the immutable reservation and checks all durable input
claims before reporting evidence for its exact lock transaction. It reports
confirmed (block hash and depth), confirmed-output-only evidence, mempool,
explicitly wallet-reported conflict, or
unobserved (with confirmed/mempool input availability). All results bind to an
unchanged chain tip. These observations never authorize a retry or replacement.
Mempool state can change independently of the chain tip.

Wallet transaction bytes must match every reserved unsigned field; positive
confirmations must match the corresponding block header's active-chain depth.
This lookup remains usable after the shared contract output itself is spent.
Missing-wallet and missing-mempool responses are handled only for the two
selected lookup RPCs, with matching response ID, numeric error -5 and null
result with Core's HTTP 500 status. Authentication, transport, malformed replies and other daemon failures
remain errors. The RPC behavior was checked against Litecoin Core 0.21.5.8
[src/wallet/rpcwallet.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/litecoin-project/litecoin/v0.21.5.8/src/wallet/rpcwallet.cpp)
and [src/rpc/blockchain.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/litecoin-project/litecoin/v0.21.5.8/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp).

The isolated harness now checks the unbroadcast reservation, broadcast-before-
confirmation, confirmation, invalidation/reconfirmation of the funding block,
and funding observation after settlement/restart. A separate competing payment
spends reserved inputs without creating the intended lock: both before and
after its confirmation, reconciliation must report the intended transaction as
unobserved with unavailable inputs. Negative unit cases cover optional lookup
errors and altered transaction identity/principal. This extends the existing
four real-chain settlement paths; it is not a negotiated LTC/XMZ swap.

Next: restore all pending wallet reservations before new coin selection, bind
signing to negotiated terms and pre-signed recovery transactions, then persist
signed bytes before any broadcast. The new observations provide recovery
evidence for that path but do not implement signing or relay themselves.

Claude's reconciliation review prompted two additional distinctions: the
unobserved result retains whether the wallet holds transaction history, and a
confirmed-output result can establish the exact lock UTXO when that wallet
history is missing. The mempool is queried again after input inspection to
reduce races; results remain point-in-time evidence, never permission to
release claims. The wallet-reported-conflict result does not assert independently
verified conflict proof. The fixture removes/restores one funding transaction
from the disposable wallet with `removeprunedfunds`/`importprunedfunds` to test
reconciliation while chain history remains intact.

The reviewed reconciliation implementation passed both machines' all-feature/
all-target builds, 96 local / 99 CachyOS library tests (2 explicit external
fixtures ignored), all four real Litecoin settlement paths plus competing-spend
and missing-wallet-history checks, and ordered source-patch verification.
Evidence on each machine: `build/litecoin-reconciliation-build.log`,
`build/litecoin-reconciliation-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-reconciliation-reviewed-chain.log`, and
`build/litecoin-reconciliation-reviewed-results.json`.
The wallet-reported-negative-confirmations branch is deliberately labelled as
wallet evidence; independent conflict proof and a dedicated fixture for that
branch remain outstanding. Existing BTC source paths and execution gates were
not changed by this milestone.


## Litecoin recovery-gated durable signing

`sign_reserved_lock` now rebuilds cancellation and full-refund transactions from
the immutable reserved PSBT and trusted recovery policy. Contract keys must
reproduce the reserved P2WSH script; the refund address must belong to the funding
wallet. Both recovery transactions must match the expected txids, witness script,
ordered signatures and SIGHASH_ALL digests. Policy binds cancel height, fees,
minimum output amounts and minimum relay fee rate. New signing checks the local
node's current relay floor. These policy floors cannot guarantee future relay
acceptance if network policy or fee conditions change.

Before requesting funding signatures, it durably stores the verified recovery
package and policy. Wallet RPC may sign only the exact reserved unsigned
transaction. Finalized funding is checked with `testmempoolaccept` and persisted
before returning. No broadcast occurs in this API. Reopening the signed record
returns exactly the retained bytes and restores volatile coin locks; a lost
signing response can only re-sign that same unsigned txid. A changed but otherwise
valid policy conflicts with the immutable signing record.

The recovery package remains in private files: publishing a decrypted refund
signature prematurely may reveal the native adaptor secret to the counterparty.
No raw recovery transactions or wallet credentials enter public logs. The fixture
exporter accepts the package through bounded private files, and exercises the
production signer in place of its previous direct wallet-signing calls.

The first negative test accidentally replaced an already-zero locktime byte;
its failure correctly exposed that the transaction had not been modified. The
corrected test corrupts the witness script explicitly. Additional cases corrupt
the DER signature's scalar, change the sighash, fee/timelock/destination/key,
and alter an otherwise-valid policy after persistence. The fixture removes only
its disposable `.signed` receipt to simulate interruption between the two durable
records, then checks identical funding identity on retry. Reopening after a daemon
restart must restore input locks and return byte-identical saved funding.

Claude's read-only review verified the contract/signature construction and found
the missing coin-lock restoration on the saved-record path; that is corrected.
Recovery fee/output floors were added, and failed temporary writes are cleaned up.

This signer accepts trusted caller policy, not an authenticated peer quote. It is
not exposed by the live GUI. Still required: Litecoin commercial quote and proof
negotiation, durable peer context, whole-wallet startup coordination, and relay/
acknowledgement recovery before enabling a real LTC/XMZ market. Existing BTC paths
remain unchanged; the broader XMR/DOGE/ETH/native RUNE objective is still active.

Validated on both machines: all-feature/all-target swap-machine builds,
96 local / 99 CachyOS library tests (2 explicit external fixtures ignored),
all four real Litecoin settlement branches using durable funding signing,
negative recovery-package cases, interrupted-signing retry and restart/coin-lock
restoration, and ordered engine patch verification. Evidence on each machine:
`build/litecoin-signing-build.log`, `build/litecoin-signing-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-signing-reviewed-chain.log`, and
`build/litecoin-signing-reviewed-results.json`.
The first unsuccessful harness run is explained above; the reviewed result files
are the authoritative passing runs. Signing does not activate any live market.


## Litecoin durable relay and explicit recovery

`relay_reserved_lock` loads the immutable reservation, verified recovery package
and signed funding bytes, checks the caller's expected txid and input claims,
restores Core coin locks and checks current mempool acceptance. It synchronizes a
relay intent containing trade, chain, wallet, txid and witness identity before
sending. A missing/invalid acknowledgement returns an uncertain outcome with the
original txid. Successful acknowledgement remains successful even if saving its
receipt fails; that persistence failure is reported separately. Reopening an
existing attempt returns reconciliation-required and does not send again.

`resume_reserved_relay` is an explicit recovery operation. It observes the exact
lock first. If already in the mempool or chain, it returns that evidence without
sending. If unobserved with its original inputs still available, it revalidates
all stored records, restores input locks and retransmits only the original signed
bytes. It cannot replace inputs, reprice or create a second payment. All local
record errors remain failures requiring inspection; no error grants authority to
create another lock. Corrupt/missing recovery records are not bypassed merely
because an old relay intent exists. Caller-owned quote approval and durable peer
state remain mandatory prerequisites outside this API.

The harness forwards RPC through an owned loopback proxy. It verifies a reply
lost after real acceptance; a request dropped before reaching the node; receipt
persistence failure after acceptance; and application/daemon restarts. It counts
actual upstream sends and asserts the original relay intent remains unchanged.
Ordinary replay never sends twice. Explicit recovery restores wallet locks and
finishes an unsent request using the original signed transaction. Accepted funding
is reconciled without a second upstream send. The first harness attempt used
`expected_txid` instead of the strict exporter's `expectedTxid` request field and
was rejected before relay; that fixture naming error was corrected.

Claude's read-only review identified the unsent-request recovery gap in the first
single-attempt implementation; the explicit recovery operation addresses it.
Receipt absence is not a funding failure and acknowledgement is not confirmation.
The GUI still exposes no live execution for these markets. Litecoin quote/proof
negotiation and whole-wallet startup coordination remain before activation;
XMR, DOGE, ETH and native RUNE settlement remain part of the active objective.

Validation passed locally and on CachyOS: all-feature/all-target builds,
96 / 99 library tests respectively (2 explicit external fixtures ignored),
all four Litecoin settlement branches through the signed-funding relay API,
request-loss/reply-loss/receipt-failure and restart recovery checks, and ordered
source-patch verification. Evidence on each machine:
`build/litecoin-relay-build.log`, `build/litecoin-relay-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-relay-chain.log`, and `build/litecoin-relay-results.json`.
The successful result files were created only after the corrected request schema
and explicit unsent-request recovery tests passed. No live market is enabled.


## Signed LTC/XMZ commercial quotes

`litecoin_quote::VerifiedLtcQuote` adds a separate LTC/XMZ signature domain with
caller-pinned identities for both funders. Quotes contain exact string-encoded
principals, destinations, genesis/network identities, funding caps, per-path fees
(including cooperative early refund), output/relay floors, confirmation policy,
relative timeouts, expiry, and quote/trade identities. Canonical BTreeMap encoding
is checked independently of serde_json map ordering. Unknown/missing fields,
duplicate keys, whitespace/noncanonical integers, wrong identities/domains,
invalid addresses, unsupported app fees and deployment/policy mismatch reject.
Each current one-input/one-output recovery path has a conservative 256-vbyte fee
floor; actual cancel/refund signature sizes are checked again by the signer.

`sign_reserved_lock_for_quote` checks the reserved trade, principal and fee cap,
derives recovery terms from the verified quote, and retains the entire signed
quote before signing. The signing record binds a hash of that retained record;
relay rejects a missing/changed quote. A second otherwise-valid quote with a
changed XMZ amount cannot reprice an existing reservation. First relay checks
retained quote expiry against the system clock. Recovery after an existing relay
intent is not blocked merely by commercial quote expiry.

The real-node harness uses Python/libsodium to sign the complete quote, with Rust
verifying it and using it for funding signing. Both roles use fixed public test
identities. The harness rejects validly signed wrong-principal, expired and wrong-
genesis quotes; invalid signatures; later repricing; and missing quote records.
Its XMZ genesis/address are explicit synthetic quote fixtures: this establishes
commercial binding, not native-chain funding or cross-curve proof negotiation.
Unit cases also sign malformed canonical encodings with both valid keys so their
rejection cannot be attributed only to signature mismatch. BTC quote/signature
paths are unchanged and reject the LTC-domain payload.

Claude's review identified exact-quote persistence and initial-relay expiry gaps
in the first draft; both are addressed. Redeem/punish and early-refund fee floors
are enforced along with cancellation/refund floors. Fresh-quote verification is
not used as a gate for historical transaction reconciliation. Still required:
authenticated LTC/XMZ proof and transaction exchange, whole-wallet startup
coordination, GUI quote/approval and engine transport wiring, complete native-leg
tests, and production network validation before activating the LTC market.

Validated on both machines: all-feature/all-target builds; 101 local / 104
CachyOS library tests (2 explicit external fixtures ignored); independent
libsodium-signed quotes driving all four real Litecoin settlement paths;
immutable quote binding, absent-record rejection, lost-request/reply recovery,
and ordered engine patch verification. Evidence on each machine:
`build/litecoin-quote-build.log`, `build/litecoin-quote-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-quote-chain.log`, and `build/litecoin-quote-results.json`.
The stricter validly-signed noncanonical-payload cases were added after the
all-target build and passed the all-feature library suite on both hosts.
No LTC or other new market is executable in the GUI yet.

### LTC/XMZ authenticated key phase

Added a separate quote-bound two-frame key exchange using the existing engine's
cross-curve proof system. Each role signs canonical frames containing the quote
commitment, swap ID, sequence and previous-frame commitment. Validation rejects
wrong roles, altered context, expired quotes, noncanonical encodings, invalid
proofs, degenerate native keys and key reuse across roles without advancing the
cursor. Both peers derive the same Litecoin contract and XMZ shared destination.
Frames include private view shares and must never appear in public logs.

This is an in-memory key phase, not funding authorization. Durable secret/cursor
storage, recovery-transaction exchange, binding the validated keys into the
funding driver, and an end-to-end native-chain swap remain outstanding. The
existing settlement harness still uses independent fixed contract fixtures;
its passing chain tests do not prove the new negotiation drives settlement.

All-feature/all-target builds passed on both machines, with 103 local and 106
CachyOS library tests passing (2 external fixtures ignored on each). All four
existing Litecoin isolated-chain settlement paths passed on both machines.
Evidence: `build/litecoin-negotiation-build.log`,
`build/litecoin-negotiation-unit-tests.log`,
`build/litecoin-negotiation-chain.log`,
`build/litecoin-negotiation-results.json` and
`build/litecoin-negotiation-patches.log`.
All new markets remain disabled.

Claude review prompted an additional local-role/held-secret binding: each
exchange now receives its local role and `LocalKeys`, and refuses a signed local
frame containing any other key share. A regression test supplies a validly
signed replacement share and verifies rejection. Frame decoding errors are
sanitized to avoid echoing private view shares. The review's quote parsing
concerns are already excluded by the private `VerifiedLtcQuote` constructor:
exact lowercase identity bytes, distinct pins, canonical UUIDs and canonical
positive numeric strings are enforced before exchange construction. Transcript
completion is not mutual funding approval; later transaction exchange must
bind its commitment. Secret zeroization and persistent state remain unfinished.

### Funding bound to validated LTC/XMZ keys

`sign_reserved_lock_for_exchange` now derives recovery keys from `VerifiedKeys`,
checks the reservation's contract against the negotiated address, validates the
signed recovery transactions, and retains a public exchange binding before
wallet signing. The signing journal hashes this binding; relay rejects missing
or changed binding records. Private view shares are excluded from the public
binding. Existing low-level signing APIs remain trusted-caller interfaces.

The chain harness now runs the two-peer key exchange using public deterministic
fixture secrets matching the independent swap-core transaction builder. Its
funding calls use the exchange-aware signer and test absent/altered exchange
records before relay. This connects proof negotiation to the real Litecoin
funding and recovery transactions, but still does not fund or settle an XMZ leg.
The fixture imports secrets explicitly; production must durably preserve keys
and original proof/frame bytes, rather than regenerate an exchange on restart.
Imported zero/out-of-range spend scalars are rejected before proof generation.

All-feature/all-target builds and library tests passed locally (104 tests) and
on CachyOS (107 tests), with 2 external fixtures ignored per host. Evidence uses
`build/litecoin-key-binding-*`; chain regression and review results are recorded
separately below when complete. New markets remain non-executable.

Review follow-up: signing wrappers now preflight the complete prospective
signing record before retaining quote/exchange metadata, while holding one
journal lock through the signing operation. This prevents a rejected upgrade
from quote-only signing from making its old relay record unusable. The harness
simulates that upgrade and checks that no exchange file is left behind. The
exchange-aware signer also requires the local Litecoin-funder role. Deployment
selection is already bound by the same immutable verified quote and its policy
checks. These follow-up changes are undergoing the updated chain regression.

CachyOS completed all four exchange-bound Litecoin settlement paths in

are active on both hosts and use `build/litecoin-key-binding-final-chain.log`
and `build/litecoin-key-binding-final-results.json`. Do not treat the earlier
report as proof of those subsequent fixes. The final local build and 104 library
tests passed; CachyOS is rebuilding and repeating its suite before that run.

### Original key/proof checkpoint codec

Added explicit sensitive key checkpoints bound to the signed quote commitment
and local role. Restoration reconstructs public keys from the secret scalars,
checks them against every advertised share, validates the original cross-curve
proof, and retains that proof rather than regenerating it. Returned checkpoint
buffers zeroize on drop; serializer copies and all key objects are not claimed
to be fully zeroized. These bytes contain spending secrets and require private
storage. The codec does not yet provide durable files, accepted-frame cursor
restoration, or funding approval.

Four targeted negotiation tests passed on both machines, including exact
original-frame reproduction after restoration, wrong-role rejection and
corrupted-secret rejection. Evidence: `build/litecoin-secret-state-tests.log`
and `build/litecoin-secret-state-patches.log`. Only the library test target was
rebuilt during the ongoing final chain runs, keeping their wallet fixture
binaries unchanged. All-target compilation of the added codec remains pending.

### Accepted-frame transcript restoration

The exchange now retains its accepted signed frames and can export a sensitive
transcript checkpoint with an integrity commitment. Restoration reconstructs
its cursor by revalidating each original frame/signature/proof under the saved
quote context and admission times. It checks the recorded final predecessor and
sequence, rejects replay after restoration, and still rejects new acceptance
after quote expiry. A supplied trusted checkpoint commitment rejects stale or
altered bytes. A hash stored beside an old checkpoint alone does not prevent
rollback: durable latest-state ownership remains a driver requirement.

Five targeted negotiation tests passed locally. CachyOS passed the updated
all-feature/all-target build and full library suite: 109 passed, 2 external
fixtures ignored. Evidence: local `build/litecoin-transcript-state-tests.log`;
CachyOS `build/litecoin-transcript-state-build.log` and
`build/litecoin-transcript-state-unit-tests.log`; both hosts
`build/litecoin-transcript-state-patches.log`. Local all-target compilation of
the codecs remains deferred until its existing chain run finishes, so its
wallet test binary remains unchanged during that run.

CachyOS's final exchange-bound chain regression completed successfully,
including all four settlement paths and rejected legacy-record upgrades:
`build/litecoin-key-binding-final-results.json`. It explicitly reports
`fullCrossChainSettlement:false`, `executable:false`, and `mwebActive:false`.
The equivalent local run remains active; its process is executing wallet proof
fixtures and has completed redeem/refund. Persistent private storage, atomic
cursor advancement with the execution journal, recovery transaction exchange,
and native XMZ funding/recovery integration are still required.

### Private immutable exchange checkpoint storage

Added Linux private storage for the key and transcript checkpoints using the
existing descriptor-anchored journal: owner-only directories/files, exclusive
locking, bounded reads, no symlink following, immutable publication, file fsync
and directory fsync. Restore requires the exact commitment from the caller's
trusted execution record. Missing state is an error; it never scans for an
older checkpoint, regenerates keys, or starts a new exchange. The execution
driver must still atomically record that latest commitment before acknowledging
progress or funding. Storage alone is not rollback protection or approval.

The real filesystem test reopens partial/completed exchanges, checks private
permissions, rejects mismatched keys before any write, rejects the wrong role
and unsafe directory permissions, and refuses fallback when the committed
checkpoint is missing. All-feature/all-target builds and full library suites

### Durable outgoing key frames

Added `prepare_outgoing` and `load_outgoing` over the private journal. Preparation
loads an exact stored checkpoint, checks the signing identity against the quote
pin, constructs only the local frame, validates it, and retains its exact signed
bytes before returning. A single immutable record per trade/role prevents a
retry from substituting another checkpoint or frame. Recovery can load the
original bytes without the identity secret; it does not send them or authorize
funding. The saved frame contains private view material and has no Debug or
public serialization interface.

retries/recovery (including after expiry), recovery after dropping the identity
secret and in-memory exchange, checkpoint mismatch rejection, and malformed
record rejection. Local all-feature/all-target build and full library suite
passed: 108 tests, 2 external fixtures ignored. CachyOS full library suite
passed: 111 tests, 2 ignored. Its outgoing-state all-target build remains deferred
until the ongoing chain fixture finishes, preserving that binary during the
run. Evidence: `build/litecoin-outgoing-state-build.log` locally,
`build/litecoin-outgoing-state-tests.log` and
`build/litecoin-outgoing-state-patches.log` on both machines.

The latest CachyOS chain run (`build/litecoin-private-state-chain.log`) is still

### Cold-start signed quote recovery

Transcript checkpoints now include the original signed quote record. Cold-start
storage recovery takes the trade UUID, exact trusted checkpoint commitment,
pinned signer identities and deployment configuration, then revalidates the
stored quote under its committed historical admission policy/time. It restores
the original terms without refreshing their expiry or bypassing current funding
limits. Full record canonicality, signatures, quote commitment, trade identity,
local keys and transcript context are checked before recovery returns.

The filesystem test discards the original quote/keys/exchange, reloads them from
private records, and verifies that expired funding and tightened current limits
still reject execution. Wrong pins and changed deployment identity also fail.

### Recovery of retained outgoing-frame acceptance

Added `recover_outgoing_acceptance` to restore the state immediately before a
retained outgoing key frame, revalidate that frame at its original admission
time, and durably retain the successor checkpoint under the same journal lock.
It does not regenerate/re-sign, require fresh quote admission, assert peer
receipt, or authorize funding. Repeating recovery from the same predecessor
returns the identical successor. Passing the successor as another predecessor
is rejected by the outgoing record's original checkpoint binding.

The existing real-filesystem outgoing-frame regression now covers this crash
window, verifies that replay is rejected in the restored successor, and compares
the recovered successor with normal local acceptance. Both all-feature/all-target
builds and full library suites passed: 109 local / 112 CachyOS, with 2 external
fixtures ignored per host. Evidence on both hosts:
`build/litecoin-outgoing-recovery-build.log`,
`build/litecoin-outgoing-recovery-tests.log`, and
`build/litecoin-outgoing-recovery-patches.log`.

The driver must still commit the returned successor in its trusted latest-state
metadata before proceeding. Existing BTC execution claims/checkpoint pin stores
provide a reference for that ownership layer; they have not been changed or
reused across chain domains here. Full LTC/XMZ execution, authenticated recovery
transaction exchange, and native-leg tests remain unfinished. New markets stay
disabled.

### Owned key-phase execution controller

Added `litecoin_negotiation::execution::Execution`. It requires a reviewed quote
commitment to begin, retains a single-use attempt marker, exclusively owns a
private metadata directory, and stores secret snapshots in a separate private
directory. The current checkpoint is selected by an atomically replaced head
record, not by scanning for the newest snapshot. Missing committed state fails
closed; it cannot start a second attempt or select an older checkpoint.

Outgoing frames and their local acceptance are retained before returning bytes
for transport. Peer frames and admission times are retained before acknowledging
receipt, so interrupted incoming and outgoing operations can be recovered after
expiry without fresh signing or another delivery. Duplicate committed peer
frames are idempotent; conflicting duplicates are rejected. State transitions
require `&mut self` so a shared controller cannot interleave competing commits
in safe Rust. The journal lock protects compare/replace across controllers;
head contents and the directory are re-synced before retry success, covering a
prior rename followed by directory-sync failure.

The controller is a key-phase library API, not yet GUI/network/wallet execution
wiring or funding authority. Recovery transaction negotiation and native XMZ
funding/settlement remain separate unfinished steps. Its lifecycle test drives
both peers, restarts after retained outgoing and incoming frames before head
publication, checks expired retry/recovery, completes identical transcripts,
rejects a competing owner/repeated attempt, and rejects a missing committed
snapshot. One metadata directory serializes one wallet's controller operations.

### Two-party Litecoin recovery signature primitive

Added `litecoin_negotiation::recovery::RecoveryPlan`.
It derives cancel/full-refund/punish digests from the signed quote, verified
key exchange and supplied lock PSBT.
It checks input metadata cardinality, duplicate/null inputs, native SegWit
funding, stable scriptSig/non-RBF inputs, any supplied previous transaction,
checked fee arithmetic, exact contract principal and refund/payout scripts.
Witness UTXO descriptions are not chain evidence: the funding driver must
still check this PSBT against its owned reservation and node.

Alice supplies the cancel signature and a full-refund adaptor signature
encrypted to Bob's native spend key.
Bob supplies cancel and punish signatures.
Canonical bounded frames are signed by the pinned role identities and bind
the quote, key transcript, lock outpoint and every recovery transaction ID.
Each recipient verifies the peer's identity and contract signatures before
combining them with only its own local secrets.
Wrong role/keys/identity, altered binding, invalid adaptor/cancel signatures,
malformed funding and expired quote construction are rejected.

### Durable recovery controller integration (validation running)

`Execution` now provides `prepare_recovery`, `recover_recovery_outgoing`,
`accept_recovery` and `recover_recovery`.
A private immutable intent retains the exact PSBT, completed key checkpoint,
admission policy and time.
Its SHA-256 digest is committed into the execution head before any recovery
signature is returned.
A missing or altered committed intent causes cold resume to fail.
An interrupted intent-to-head publication may only resume the same PSBT.

Outgoing canonical identity-signed frames are synced before being returned;
identity-free recovery verifies the retained identity and contract signatures.
New signatures require fresh quote admission; retries of retained signatures
can recover after expiry without granting fresh funding authority.
Peer frames are verified using the original key state, then retained before
completed transactions are published.
If publication is interrupted, cold recovery revalidates the retained peer
frame and deterministically reconstructs the same recovery transactions.

spend/view keys to reproduce the exact negotiated XMZ address.

automatic serialization. This does not claim all intermediate copies are erased.
Key possession is not chain confirmation or authorization to broadcast.

## Dogecoin confirmation adapter — 5 October 2026

`swap-machine::dogecoin_rpc::DogecoinRpc` adds a read-only loopback node
boundary for confirmed legacy transactions. It binds the configured Dogecoin
network and genesis, requires a synchronized node, checks exact transaction
bytes/identity and the requested active block, cross-checks depth against block
height, and rejects observations spanning a changing tip. Evidence is ephemeral
and cannot be deserialized from peer assertions. Callers authenticate their node
service independently. The adapter does not establish unspentness, CLTV
activation, refund maturity or swap completion, and has no signing/relay API.

The RPC format is based on the pinned Dogecoin Core 1.14.9 sources:
[raw transactions](https://github.com/dogecoin/dogecoin/blob/v1.14.9/src/rpc/rawtransaction.cpp)
and [chain observations](https://github.com/dogecoin/dogecoin/blob/v1.14.9/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp).
Unlike the Litecoin call, Dogecoin transaction lookup takes two arguments;
spent historical transactions require the node's transaction index.

`upstream-dogecoin-observation.patch` retains this addition in the ordered
engine reconstruction. `test_dogecoin_primitives.py --observer-test-binary ...`
now checks the actual Rust observer before/after restart, rejects zero/excessive
depth and a wrong block, revokes confirmation on block invalidation, and accepts
only the new inclusion after reconfirmation.
