  passed. Existing unused-dependency/mutability warnings remain.
- Ordered patches reproduce the engine sources; Python syntax and Git whitespace

  145 passed, zero failed, seven explicitly ignored isolated-node fixtures

python3 -u tools/dex-engine-port/test_dogecoin_primitives.py \

## Explicit Litecoin startup helper — 5 October 2026

The native journal helper now exposes `--start-review-stdio-v1` and
`--start-submit-stdio-v1`. A private v5 configuration supplies a separate
`startQuoteFile` containing the existing mutually signed v2 quote envelope.
The helper validates the pinned counterparties, configured policy, quote expiry
and trade ID before producing a review. Startup approval binds the role, exact
terms and policy; it is distinct from payment approval. The helper requires
Litecoin regtest. Review does not open the execution journal or generate keys.

Submission calls the existing `Execution::begin_reviewed` owner API. Repeated
startup cannot replace keys or overwrite an attempted trade: callers must resume
its retained state, including after a lost reply. V5 grants no wallet-RPC or
payment authority. A separate funding/payout/refund configuration and explicit
approval are still required. The Qt/QML startup interface remains unfinished.

`upstream-litecoin-start-helper.patch` retains the helper and fixture extension.
The three helper request/configuration/privacy tests and the existing startup
approval test passed; all-features/all-targets compilation and ordered patch
reconstruction also passed. The paired-chain harness has a `--helper-start`
option to start both roles through separate helper processes before negotiating
keys and exercising its existing success/refund flow. It checks unchanged
reviewed terms, role-separated approvals, rejection before storage mutation and
repeated-start protection. Both actual runs passed:

- `build/litecoin-start-helper-success-20261005-results.json`: both roles began
  through the helper; subsequent GUI-bound funding and payout submission,
  confirmation and reorganisation checks passed, with exact native payout.
- `build/litecoin-start-helper-refund-20261005-results.json`: both roles began
  through the helper; changed role/policy/trade/pins and repeated-start attempts
  were rejected without altering retained state. The timeout path cancelled and
  refunded Litecoin, recovered the native wallet, and paid and confirmed the
  native refund through the existing GUI process bridge.

The fixtures set `startupHelperVerified=true` and retain `executable=false`.
Their `recoveryPathsVerified=false` means these runs are not exhaustive crash,
recovery or release acceptance. No startup control has yet been added to QML.

The first actual run exited before daemon readiness because the archived Monzero
binary needed its matching Boost 1.90 libraries. The resumed fixtures use the
existing `build/native-fixture-boost-1.90/lib` bundle in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
Only disposable regtest/fakechain funds were used; public services were unchanged.

## Qt-owned Litecoin negotiation over private TLS — 5 October 2026

`LitecoinNegotiationSession` now owns the process workflow for an approved, saved
trade: query the retained cursor, review the local frame, sign through the
unlocked encrypted identity, retain the signature, send the private message,
admit the peer frame through the helper and acknowledge durable acceptance.
Neither frames nor view shares appear in its presentation status. Configuration,
quote bytes, helper digest, request IDs and all snapshot trade fields are checked
around each helper operation. Delivery acknowledgements bind the exact frame and
signature. Process/transport failures report an unknown outcome and require a
new session using the existing saved trade.

`PrivateQuoteChannel` and its server have an explicit Litecoin negotiation
profile with bounded message/read/write queues; the original quote profile keeps
its previous limit. TLS still requires certificate validation and a separately
pinned peer certificate. The coordinator accepts only the negotiation profile.
The engine's read-only negotiation status distinguishes local/peer/completed
steps, including whether a local message has already been retained. This avoids
using failed signing attempts as a state probe. Retained frames can be redelivered
on reconnect without new keys or signing records.

`DexEngine` can attach the coordinator natively and exposes its public status to
the Litecoin page. The page distinguishes waiting for a peer, waiting for an
acknowledgement, completed key exchange and interrupted delivery. Completed key
exchange explicitly requires separate funding review and approval.

## Wallet startup provisions the Litecoin peer — 5 October 2026

The wallet accepts `--dex-ltc-peer <private-config>` together with
`--dex-ltc-journal <v5-startup-config>` under its existing private-prototype
opt-in. `LitecoinPeerStartup` owns the encrypted identity and pinned TLS setup.
It waits for `DexEngine` to report the matching saved trade before listening or
connecting. Reviewing a quote alone opens no network connection. Initial trade
approval and a validated saved-journal refresh on wallet restart can both start
negotiation. Changed configuration/credentials, a mismatched trade or identity,
non-loopback addresses and invalid ports are rejected.

Peer configuration is canonical compact JSON (sorted keys), schema
`monzero-private-ltc-peer-v1`, with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "schema": "monzero-private-ltc-peer-v1",
  "mode": "listen",
  "address": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 18446,
  "peerName": "localhost",
  "peerCertificateSha256": "<64 lowercase hex characters: other participant's TLS certificate digest>",
  "certificateFile": "/private/alice.crt",
  "privateKeyFile": "/private/alice.key",
  "caFile": "/private/trusted-ca.pem",
  "identityFile": "/private/alice-identity.bin",
  "passphraseFile": "/private/alice-password"
}
```

The example is expanded for readability; serialize it with sorted keys and no
extra whitespace before use. Paths must be canonical absolute paths to owned,
private regular files (mode 0600, no symlinks or hardlinks). The identity's parent
directory must also be private. The TLS private key is an unencrypted RSA or EC
PEM file protected by those permissions. The signing identity uses the existing
encrypted Qt identity-store format. The password file contains the exact password
bytes, with no automatically added newline. Certificate validation and the pinned
peer digest are both required; `peerName` is checked on outbound TLS connections.
The other participant uses `mode: "connect"`, the listener's port and its own
identity/certificate, with the listener's certificate digest pinned.

Start and approve the listening participant before the connecting participant.
Provision both with their own private v5 journal configuration and the matching
mutually signed quote. The existing opt-in is
`MONZERO_ENABLE_PRIVATE_DEX=I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_IS_A_LOCAL_PROTOTYPE`.
A failed connection reports an unknown outcome; restart using the same retained
trade/configuration to reconcile. Startup makes one connection attempt and never
creates a replacement trade. This remains an isolated-chain workflow, not a live
market activation mechanism.

The full wallet build, Qt engine/private-channel/settlement suites (3/3), and all
18 QML presentation checks pass. The new `--gui-peer-startup` fixture configures
both native startup owners before either trade exists, proves no listener opens
during review, approves trade creation through `DexEngine`, checks automatic TLS
negotiation, rejects credentials changed after configuration, and resumes the
same saved state after recreation. Both full paths passed:

- `build/litecoin-peer-startup-success-20261005-results.json`: native wallet
  startup, negotiation and GUI-bound funding/payout settlement.
- `build/litecoin-peer-startup-refund-20261005-results.json`: the same startup
  path, Litecoin cancellation/refund and GUI-bound native refund settlement.

Both reports set `walletPeerStartupVerified=true`,
`privateNegotiationSessionVerified=true`, `guiStartupVerified=true` and
`fullCrossChainSettlement=true` for the respective isolated path. They retain
`recoveryPathsVerified=false` and `executable=false`. The configured-before-save
presentation was captured and inspected at
`build/litecoin-peer-startup-screen-20261005.png` using a display fixture.

Negotiation provisioning is now wired into the wallet entry point. Payment
preparation/orchestration, recovery acceptance and the other currencies' remaining
settlement implementations are still unfinished. A complete interactive trading
wizard and live market activation are not established by these fixture results.


## 5 October 2026 — native XMZ funding preparation

The LTC journal helper now exposes `--funding-prepare-stdio-v1`. It prepares and
retains the XMZ lock transaction without relaying it, then returns the exact saved
payment review and commitment. Qt exposes `prepareLitecoinFunding()` and QML has
an explicit “Prepare XMZ funding (no broadcast)” control. The source wallet,
account and priority are visible. Sending still requires the separate review
checkbox and matching commitment. A lost or invalid response leaves preparation
unknown; refresh reads the retained trade before another operation.

Preparation uses the existing private journal v4 configuration with
`fundingRpcFile`. That RPC file uses `monzero-private-ltc-funding-rpc-v2` and adds
`source: {wallet: <XMZ primary address>, account: <u32>, priority: <1..4>}` to the
v1 RPC fields. The selected source is pinned in Qt and checked by the helper for
preparation, submission and confirmation. Legacy v1 RPC files do not enable the
preparation control. Configuration remains restricted to the isolated regtest
prototype; no market activation was changed.

The engine now performs its read-only wallet/account/chain preflight before
retaining a first source intent. An incorrect source therefore does not pin an
unusable funding intent. Once preparation is retained, retries restore the exact
same transaction. Completed recovery agreement, current Litecoin lock depth and
the cancellation safety window are still checked before initial preparation.
The ordered source patch is `upstream-litecoin-funding-preparation.patch`.

## 5 October 2026 — recovery agreement signed by the wallet identity

The engine now separates recovery-message construction from local identity
signing. `recovery_signing_frame` retains the exact PSBT agreement and contract
signatures before returning the message; `submit_recovery_signature` verifies
the pinned identity over exactly those bytes before publishing the outgoing
message. It rejects changed bytes and first-time signing after quote expiry.
Retained outgoing messages remain idempotent after expiry. The original
in-engine identity API delegates to this same retention path.

The private startup helper exposes `--recovery-review-stdio-v1`,
`--recovery-submit-stdio-v1` and `--recovery-accept-stdio-v1` under the existing
owned v5/regtest configuration. The first request supplies a canonical PSBT and
prepares recovery state; it is not a read-only display operation. The latter
two use bounded `frameHex`/`signatureHex` fields. Peer signatures are checked and
the completed recovery transactions are retained before acknowledgement. None
of these operations broadcasts or signs the funding lock. The funding driver
must independently validate its owned reservation before lock signing.

`OfferIdentity::signLitecoinRecovery` uses the recovery protocol's fixed domain
and a 16,384-byte limit, distinct from key-exchange signing. The Qt encrypted
identity store can now sign recovery messages without passing its identity key
into the engine. The paired-chain driver has a `--gui-recovery-signing` path
that reserves the lock, uses actual helper processes and the Qt identity signer
for both parties, and then resumes the reservation for funding. The ordered
engine patch is `upstream-litecoin-recovery-signing.patch`.

The recovery signer preserves the engine wire format: the recovery domain,
a NUL byte, an eight-byte big-endian frame length, and the frame. It deliberately
does not use the offer/key-exchange envelope. Cross-language chain testing caught
and corrected this distinction before acceptance. Qt verifies the explicit
framing and rejects empty/oversized messages and cross-protocol signatures.

Validation: wallet and Qt targets build; all three DEX CTest suites pass, with
`dex_engine` rerun after the framing correction. Rust reports 146 library tests
passed (7 ordinary-suite fixture skips), 5 helper tests passed, and a successful
release all-features/all-targets check. The extended execution lifecycle covers
retained frame equality across restart, wrong signature/domain and changed-frame
rejection, expiry rejection before first publication, and exact retry after
publication. Ordered patches reconstruct all changed engine sources.

Both full isolated paths passed with recovery signed by the Qt identity store:

- `build/litecoin-recovery-signing-success-20261005-results.json`
- `build/litecoin-recovery-signing-refund-20261005-results.json`

Both report `guiRecoverySigningVerified=true`,
`recoveryHelperAdmissionVerified=true`, `guiFundingPreparationVerified=true`
and `fullCrossChainSettlement=true`. Requests with extra authority, missing
review, wrong signatures and reflected local messages are rejected. Repeated
local publication and peer acceptance leave retained files unchanged, and the
recovery exchange leaves both transaction pools unchanged. The reserved lock is
then resumed, signed and funded before the usual success/refund flow, including
GUI funding/payout/refund approval and reorg checks.

This adds a verified helper/identity boundary, not automatic app orchestration.
Private-channel recovery delivery and Litecoin reservation provisioning still
need integration into the normal wallet flow; fixture code continues to drive
those steps and payout/refund preparation. `recoveryPathsVerified=false` and
`executable=false` remain correct. Other currencies' settlement remains unfinished.


## 5 October 2026 — private recovery exchange owned by the Qt session

`LitecoinNegotiationSession` now continues from completed key exchange into
recovery-message exchange over the existing mutually authenticated, pinned TLS
channel. The native `DexEngine::startLitecoinRecovery` entry accepts the reserved
PSBT from the Litecoin funding driver. Only the Litecoin-funder role can initiate
it, after authenticated key exchange; the native funder accepts the corresponding
private message and prepares its own bound recovery response.

For each role, the coordinator invokes helper preparation, signs using the
Qt encrypted identity, retains the signed message through the helper, and sends
it only after successful publication. It acknowledges incoming messages only
after the helper verifies and retains the completed recovery transactions. Local
and remote quote/role bindings, exact PSBT equality, helper request IDs, unchanged
saved terms, and delivery digests are checked. The recovery deadline covers both
peer-message delivery and acknowledgement. Invalid responses or interruptions
leave recovery unknown and close the channel. No funding operation is invoked.

The public status has `recoveryStarted`, `recoveryState` and `recoveryComplete`;
private message bytes and PSBTs remain outside QML. The page distinguishes
recovery preparation, waiting, completion and interruption, with separate funding
approval still required. The native entry is intended for the owned reservation
driver; provisioning that reservation and invoking the entry from the interactive
workflow remain unfinished.

The extended actual Qt session test exchanges both recovery messages, recreates
both sessions and verifies exact replay without changes to retained files. It
rejects initiation before key exchange, initiation by the wrong role, malformed
PSBTs, duplicate local starts, wrong TLS pins and invalid recovery
acknowledgements. The `--gui-recovery-session` paired-chain path uses this
coordinator instead of fixture-managed helper exchange.

## 5 October 2026 — app-owned Litecoin input reservation and recovery handoff

The new `LitecoinReservationJob` invokes the native helper to prepare or restore
Litecoin funding inputs, then passes the exact retained PSBT directly to the
private recovery session. The QML control is enabled only for the matching
Litecoin-funder trade after authenticated key exchange, while neither operation
is busy and recovery has not started. Public status includes amounts, fee limit,
wallet and transaction ID; the PSBT stays in native code. This operation reserves
inputs and exchanges recovery signatures, without signing or broadcasting the
funding transaction.

`LitecoinRpc::prepare_or_resume_lock` reads the existing immutable reservation
first. Existing intent must match the trade, deployment, contract, amount and
fee ceiling. Only an absent intent permits new coin selection; corruption,
conflicting terms or unavailable inputs fail without replacement. The shared
journal still provides exclusive input claims and restores Core's advisory coin
locks after restart. The helper verifies the fresh signed startup quote against
the saved trade and completed keys before reservation. An expired quote is
rejected by this preparation entry; it does not authorize replacement funding.

Native wallet startup accepts `--dex-ltc-reservation <owned-config>` alongside
`--dex-ltc-journal` (v5), `--dex-ltc-peer`, and the existing explicit prototype
opt-in. The wrapper is canonical compact sorted JSON, owned mode 0600:

```json
{"journalConfigFile":"/absolute/startup.json","rpcFile":"/absolute/reservation-rpc.json","schema":"monzero-private-ltc-reservation-v1"}
```

The private RPC file has exactly these fields: `schema` equal to
`monzero-private-ltc-reservation-rpc-v1`, `ltcPort`, `ltcWallet`, `ltcAnchor`,
`ltcCookieFile`, `reservationDirectory`, and positive `feeRateAtomsPerKb`.
The reservation directory must be canonical, owned and private, shared by every
trade using the exclusively owned Litecoin wallet(s). The helper remains regtest
only. The job pins configuration bytes and the helper executable digest before
and after operations. Configuration changes leave an unknown result without
starting the helper; they do not silently switch wallets or reservation storage.

## Litecoin lock funding approval — 5 October 2026

The owned reservation helper now supports `--lock-funding-review-stdio-v1` and
`--lock-funding-submit-stdio-v1` using the existing private reservation wrapper.
Review validates the saved reservation, input ownership, signed quote, negotiated
recovery transactions and any retained signing/dispatch records. It reports the
wallet, contract, refund destination, change, input count, fee ceiling, total debit,
expiry and exact transaction ID. Review does not sign, send or query chain state.

Approval commits to those details, including hashes of retained reservation,
recovery, signed transaction and dispatch records. A mismatched or stale approval
fails before signing or relay. First submission uses the existing fresh-quote
recovery-protected signing path. A prior dispatch instead reconciles and, only
when permitted by the existing observation checks, retransmits the same persisted
bytes. It cannot select replacement inputs or reprice the transaction.

`LitecoinReservationJob` pins configuration and helper bytes, validates responses,
and clears the review on submission or uncertainty. The QML control displays the
review with unchecked consent; any status/review change resets consent. Node
acknowledgement is presented separately from confirmation. Interrupted operations
require a fresh review, with no automatic replacement or payment retry.

## App preparation of recovered XMZ payments — 5 October 2026

The native helper now exposes `--payout-prepare-stdio-v1` and
`--refund-prepare-stdio-v1`. Requests contain the operation schema, request ID and
explicit `priority` (1–4), with no submission action, approval commitment or
funding safety-block field. Existing operation modes reject the new priority
field. Preparation calls the existing durable engine APIs: it observes both
chains, retains the exact signed payment with relay disabled, and returns the
existing payment review. A retained payment is restored rather than replaced;
a different priority is rejected. Already-attempted payments cannot be prepared.

Preparation requires the corresponding private RPC schema v2, retaining all v1
fields and adding `preparationObserver` with exactly `walletPort` and `loginFile`.
This is the original funding-source wallet for refunds, or the funding observer
wallet for payouts. Its port must differ from the spending wallet, Litecoin node
and native daemon. The spending-wallet connection remains the recovered claim or
refund wallet. v1 remains usable for reviewing/submitting existing payments but
cannot silently supply a preparation observer. Fakechain/regtest restrictions,
owned private files, credential leases and operation-specific roles remain in
force.

`LitecoinJournalJob` and `DexEngine` expose payout/refund preparation with explicit
priority 1. Availability requires the matching retained claim/refund and an
unprepared payment. The returned snapshot must preserve the prior trade and
change only that payment's prepared state. The returned review passes the same
commitment, amount, destination and role checks used by later approval. QML shows
preparation status, then requires separate unchecked payment consent. Unknown
outcomes require refreshing and inspecting the saved trade.

## Litecoin recovery confirmation controls — 5 October 2026

Cancellation and Litecoin refund now have separate confirmation buttons in the
DEX. `Execution::check_recovery_spend` derives the expected transaction from the
saved recovery agreement, discovers its block through the configured node's
transaction index, then uses the existing explicit-block verifier. It checks
network identity, active block membership, block/header depth agreement, decoded
transaction identity, the agreed transaction effect, the maximum of signed and
local confirmation requirements, and a stable chain tip. An alternative valid
witness published by a peer may satisfy the shared cancellation; no local
submission receipt is required. This operation grants no send authority.

The index lookup supplies only a block hint. A missing/unready index, unconfirmed
transaction, insufficient depth or reorganised block cannot produce a confirmed
result. The Qt bridge binds the response to the configured trade, quote, operation
and depth policy. Any new operation clears prior observed evidence and approvals;
a failed check leaves no confirmed transaction in the app. Confirmation evidence
is point-in-time and is not persisted as authority for another operation.

The UI distinguishes cancellation into the recovery contract from refund to the
signed destination, displays the transaction, block, observed tip and depth, and
states that this does not confirm the XMZ payment. The current check requires
`txindex=1` on the caller-owned Litecoin node; the explicit-block verifier remains
available to callers that already have a block hint. These app controls remain
restricted to the existing regtest LTC-funder configuration.

Engine changes are retained in `upstream-litecoin-recovery-confirmation.patch`.

## External Litecoin redemption identity signing — 5 October 2026

The redemption driver now supports the app's external encrypted identity signer.
`redeem_signing_frame` retains one exact adaptor-signature frame, bound to the
checkpoint, signed quote and admitted native funding proof. Both initial review
and repeat review reobserve native funding, the exact live Litecoin lock and the
cancellation safety margin before returning any frame. The unsigned frame itself
is sensitive release material and is kept on the native helper path.

`submit_redeem_signature` rechecks both chains and accepts only the exact retained
frame signed by the pinned Litecoin-funder identity under the redemption domain.
A missing, corrupt or conflicting pending record is never replaced. The pending frame is hash-pinned in the journal head before it is returned, so
a missing file on cold resume fails closed. An interrupted head publication can
finish only from the same retained frame after fresh evidence checks. The signed
release is retained before publication of its head digest. Exact resubmission is
idempotent but still checks current evidence. The existing internal signing API
uses the same retained frame and guards.

The helper adds `--redeem-review-stdio-v1` and `--redeem-submit-stdio-v1` with a
private `monzero-private-ltc-redeem-v1` wrapper containing `journalConfigFile` and
`rpcFile`. Its `monzero-private-ltc-redeem-rpc-v1` object explicitly supplies
`ltcPort`, `ltcWallet`, `ltcAnchor`, `ltcCookieFile`, `nativeDaemonPort`,
`observerWalletPort`, `observerLoginFile` and `safetyBlocks`. It requires the
existing v5 regtest Litecoin-funder configuration and a previously admitted
funding proof. Credentials stay in the helper; no identity key is supplied.
`--redeem-accept-stdio-v1` uses the native-funder's v5 journal configuration and
retains the authenticated peer release and completed transaction, without relay.

Qt `OfferIdentity::signLitecoinRedeem` uses the exact redemption domain, NUL,
big-endian length and frame encoding, with the 16 KiB limit. It is distinct from
both recovery signing and public offer signing. There is no QML exposure of the
frame or identity key. The full peer coordinator and funding-proof transport are
still to be connected; these helper/signing operations are their native boundary.
Engine changes are retained in `upstream-litecoin-redeem-signing.patch`.

There is no visual UI change in this milestone.

that paired one participant's helper with the other's pinned configuration;

## Private funding-proof and redemption session — 5 October 2026

The existing pinned mutual-TLS Litecoin coordinator now carries the funding proof
and approved redemption message after the recovery agreement. The native-funding
side explicitly requests a fresh proof from its own saved payment. The new
`--funding-proof-stdio-v1` helper operation verifies confirmation using the
configured source wallet and never sends a transaction. Its private proof is
transported to the Litecoin-funding peer, whose `--funding-proof-accept-stdio-v1`
operation verifies the proof against its own trade, recovery agreement and native
observer before retaining it.

The Litecoin side then waits for explicit local approval, bound to the verified
native funding transaction ID. No adaptor frame is prepared during that wait.
The screen shows the locked LTC amount, deducted fee, signed destination, trade
and native funding transaction. Consent clears when session status changes.
After approval, the existing fresh-both-chain-gated helper produces the retained
frame, Qt's encrypted identity signs it, and the helper commits the signature
before the session sends it privately. The native-funding peer validates and
retains the completed redemption before acknowledging delivery. This exchange
never broadcasts; final Litecoin submission remains a separate operation.

Messages are bound to the trade, signed quote and expected role. Bounded queues
reject conflicting messages, acknowledgements bind exact delivery digests, and
changed configurations/helper bytes fail closed. Duplicate accepted messages may
replay their delivery acknowledgement; these acknowledgements do not claim fresh
chain confirmation. Fresh sessions repeat helper validation. Funding proofs,
adaptor frames and signatures are not exposed through the QML status object.
Interrupted delivery leaves an unknown state and requires reconnecting with the
same saved trade, without automatic funding or broadcast retries.

Private startup configuration `monzero-private-ltc-peer-v2` adds
`settlementConfigFile` to the existing v1 fields; v1 remains supported. For the
native-funding role it points to a v4 funding journal configuration for the same
trade, metadata/snapshot directories, policy and identity pins. For the
Litecoin-funding role it points to the private redemption wrapper bound to the
same v5 startup journal. Every operation uses the helper pinned by its own
configuration. The current setup remains loopback/regtest-only.

to verified legacy funding bytes, active-block confirmation and `gettxout` with

## 6 October 2026 — BTC/XMR second-leg approval audit

The current engine source at `core/build/eigenwallet-engine-port` was inspected
before selecting the second-leg integration point. This is a source audit,
not an implemented or verified Monero route.

`swap/src/cli/api/request.rs::buy_xmr` acquires the swap lock before maker
selection and calls `determine_btc_to_swap`. Its selection callback receives
only `QuoteWithAddress` and displays the maker maximum as
`SelectMakerDetails::btc_amount_to_swap`. The actual selected lock amount is
`min(max_giveable, quote.max_quantity)` inside `determine_btc_to_swap`.
A route review therefore needs the selected amount and estimated lock fee,
not merely the maker's advertised maximum. The selection loop drops pending
approvals when balance or quotes change; an external bridge must preserve
that cancellation behavior and reject replies to superseded requests.

`swap/src/cli/api/tauri_bindings.rs::TauriHandle` stores its approval map only
with the Tauri feature enabled. Without that feature, `request_approval` and
`resolve_approval` return errors and `get_pending_approvals` returns an empty
list. Moreover, `Option<TauriHandle>::request_maker_selection` rejects `None`,
whereas `Option<TauriHandle>::request_bitcoin_approval` returns `Ok(true)` for
`None`. Bypassing maker selection alone would consequently bypass the later
Bitcoin lock approval. An empty pending-approval list is not evidence of consent.

`swap/src/protocol/bob/swap.rs`, in `BobState::SwapSetupCompleted`, constructs
and signs the Bitcoin lock before requesting approval, and publishes only on
an affirmative response. Its `LockBitcoinDetails` includes the actual lock
amount, network fee, Monero receive amount and receive pool, swap ID, amnesty
amount and full-refund-signature availability. This later review is necessary
because negotiated proceeds can differ from the earlier quote. A Monzero route
must retain this separate approval and must not replace it with leg-one consent.

The next implementation boundary is a transport-independent approval service
used by both maker selection and Bitcoin lock publication. The Qt adapter must
bind each request to the route leg, engine swap ID and exact reviewed terms;
missing transport, expired/cancelled requests, disconnects and stale replies must
not approve publication. The service needs tests for quote/balance invalidation,
duplicate resolution and cancellation before it can be connected to a funded
route. Persisted per-leg ownership, bounded BTC spending, independently reviewed
XMR destinations/minimum proceeds and restart reconciliation remain prerequisites.
No engine behavior, live trade capability, wallet or miner was changed by this
audit. Blockchain fixture nodes remain stopped.

## 6 October 2026 — route approval queue foundation

`swap-machine/src/route_approval.rs` adds an in-memory approval session for the
planned BTC/XMR route adapter. Each immutable review includes its route, leg,
engine swap ID, maker-selection or Bitcoin-lock purpose, exact details, random
request ID and expiry. A SHA-256 commitment covers the entire request. Replies
must echo that commitment and can be resolved only once in the owning session.
Requests are bounded to 64 per session, 32 KiB of details and five minutes.

Dropping a waiter, aborting its execution, explicitly invalidating the session,
or dropping the client session cancels unconsumed consent. Cancellation and
expiry also reject a positive reply already queued but not consumed. Waiters
retain the pending store without retaining the owning client session, so a
client disconnect can revoke consent by dropping that session. A fresh review
is required after cancellation or restart.

This service is not yet connected to `swap` maker selection, Bitcoin publication
or Qt. It does not validate quote economics, establish durable route ownership,
or itself authorize a transaction. The adapter must validate typed terms,
invalidate reviews when state changes and recheck state before publication.
The existing no-Tauri automatic approval behavior remains unchanged; it must not
be used to enable a route. No live market or funding capability was enabled.

Ten focused queue tests passed, including identity/terms commitment coverage,
duplicate and cross-session replies, task cancellation, session destruction,
expiry and cancellation after a queued positive reply. `swap-machine` compiled
with all features and all targets, and ordered patch reconstruction passed.
Evidence: `build/route-approval-tests-20261006.log`,
`build/route-approval-check-20261006.log`, and
`build/route-approval-patch-audit-20261006.log`.
The source is retained in `tools/dex-engine-port/upstream-route-approval.patch`.

## 6 October 2026 — libiconv compiler compatibility

The pinned libiconv 1.17 uses pre-C23 unprototyped declarations. Its build failed
under this machine's GCC 16 default mode with conflicting `mbrtowc` declarations.
GCC documents the changed default and parameter-list behavior in its
[porting notes](https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-15/porting_to.html).

`monero-sys/build.rs::patch_libiconv_recipe` applies a retained patch to the
copied dependency recipe, selecting GNU C17 for libiconv on Linux. It accepts
only the pinned original recipe or its exact patched result, preserving unknown
local edits by failing. The recipe content changes the dependency cache key;
no existing build cache was cleaned and no submodule revision changed.
`upstream-xmr-libiconv-c17.patch` retains this change and the embedded recipe patch.

The patched libiconv build completed and produced
`libiconv-1.17-b08eaaec489.tar.gz` with `lib/libiconv.a` and `lib/libcharset.a`.
Its cached SHA-256 manifest verified successfully
(`build/xmr-libiconv-cache-check-20261006.log`). Ordered patch reconstruction
also passed (`build/xmr-libiconv-patch-audit-20261006.log`). The full BTC/XMR
library check subsequently stopped while configuring eudev because `gperf` is
missing (`build/xmr-engine-c17-build-20261006.log`). The process exited with
status 101 and was not restarted; this is not a completed engine build or a

## 6 October 2026 — direct XMZ/XMR source audit

While direct-versus-routed clarification remains pending, the current XMZ and
XMR consensus validation paths were inspected without changing either chain.
The inspected consensus files are unmodified relative to XMZ core commit
`c4f2cc7c1bdc6f44a8d854ee0d733db715f3b8d3` and the pinned Monero commit
`dbbccecc89e1121762a4ad6b531638ece82aa0c7`.

Both `cryptonote_basic.h` files declare legacy `txout_to_script` and
`txout_to_scripthash` variants. Those declarations are not evidence that scripts
are usable: `get_output_public_key` accepts only `txout_to_key` and
`txout_to_tagged_key`, returning false otherwise. `check_outs_valid` calls this
function, and the core transaction semantic checks reject transactions when
that output validation fails. The XMZ functions are in
`monero/src/cryptonote_basic/cryptonote_format_utils.cpp` at lines 1000 and 1057,
with the core rejection at `monero/src/cryptonote_core/cryptonote_core.cpp:869`.
The corresponding XMR locations are under
`core/build/eigenwallet-engine-port/monero-sys/monero`, at lines 866 and 923 of
`src/cryptonote_basic/cryptonote_format_utils.cpp`, and line 842 of
`src/cryptonote_core/cryptonote_core.cpp`.

Both `Blockchain::is_tx_spendtime_unlocked` implementations compare the saved
unlock value with height or time. That check delays spending; it does not encode
an alternative refund recipient or the existing swap engine's cancellation path.
By contrast, `swap-core/src/bitcoin.rs::build_shared_output_descriptor` builds
a Bitcoin P2WSH shared-key output, and `bitcoin/cancel.rs::TxCancel::new`
constructs a version-2 Bitcoin transaction with the agreed input sequence and
a SegWit signature hash. These are concrete Bitcoin dependencies, not ticker
labels that can be changed to XMZ.

Consequently the current BTC/XMR implementation cannot be relabelled as a direct
XMZ/XMR implementation. This audit does not prove all direct protocols impossible,
and it does not authorize changing consensus or adding custody. A proposed
direct protocol still needs an explicit settlement and refund construction,
including recovery when either participant disappears after funding, restart
ownership, confirmation/reorganization handling and tests on both chains.
No direct protocol, chain-backed test or live trade capability was added here.
The current-status table now reflects the pending design clarification rather
than treating the earlier routed plan as the active implementation decision.

## 6 October 2026 — Dogecoin parent identity and dependent refund constraint

Added `dogecoin::tests::alternate_parent_signature_invalidates_presigned_refund`
to the engine's existing refund primitive tests. It constructs two legacy funding
transactions with identical inputs/outputs except for their P2PKH signatures.
Both signatures verify against the same signature hash and are low-S, but the
transaction IDs differ. The current refund signer rejects the alternate parent
under the original terms. A refund signature verifies for its original parent
and fails after changing its input to the alternate parent ID. A new refund can
be signed against the alternate parent by the existing one-key primitive.

This demonstrates a funding-signer replacement constraint, not a third-party
malleability exploit or consensus/mempool acceptance test: the funding input is
synthetic and no node was started. It also does not solve two-party settlement.
`TimelockedRefund` still has no counterparty redemption path. Future DOGE/XMZ
negotiation must explicitly establish recoverability for the accepted funding
identity before native exposure, and explain recovery if a needed peer disappears
or a reorganisation changes that identity. Merely changing a pre-signed refund's
outpoint cannot preserve its signature. The one-key primitive's ability to sign
again must not be assumed for a future multi-party recovery transaction.

## 6 October 2026 — Dogecoin reference protocol suitability

Reviewed BasicSwap source at commit
`277b46b0278f1cc76199f7e847988647a1b36e38`, obtained from its GitHub master commit
endpoint, rather than inferring pair support from its supported-asset list.
The source snapshot and SHA-256 manifest are retained under

In [chainparams.py](https://github.com/basicswap/basicswap/blob/277b46b0278f1cc76199f7e847988647a1b36e38/basicswap/chainparams.py#L53),
both DOGE and XMR belong to `scriptless_coins`.
[BasicSwap.validateSwapType](https://github.com/basicswap/basicswap/blob/277b46b0278f1cc76199f7e847988647a1b36e38/basicswap/basicswap.py#L3829)
selects the scripted side after reversing the roles where needed, then rejects
an adaptor swap when both assets are in its scriptless/non-SegWit categories.
Its alternative swap-type branch also rejects assets designated adaptor-only;
that category includes the scriptless set. Thus this implementation rejects
DOGE/XMR in both directions. This finding concerns the inspected implementation,
not a proof that every possible direct protocol is impossible.

For Monzero, this rules out treating BasicSwap's Dogecoin support as an existing
direct DOGE/XMZ recovery construction. XMZ would still require its own validated
integration; substituting a ticker or copying Dogecoin's address/fee adapter does
not supply it. The current one-key CLTV refund and read-only observer remain
components, not a two-party protocol. No intermediary route has been selected.

funding-identity/recovery constraint demonstrated by the preceding unit test.


## 6 October 2026 — BCH direct covenant candidate and implementation boundary

The same pinned BasicSwap revision contains a direct BCH/XMR candidate.
Its [BCH covenant builder](https://github.com/basicswap/basicswap/blob/277b46b0278f1cc76199f7e847988647a1b36e38/basicswap/interface/bch/bch.py#L354)
restricts spends to one input/output, exact absolute fees and preserved token
fields. Sequence zero selects destination-checked data-signature redemption;
otherwise CSV gates forwarding to the prescribed refund contract.
`createSCLockRefundTx` constructs this forwarding spend without a peer signature.
`signTxOtVES`/`verifyTxOtVES` use the destination bytecode hash, not a transaction
signature hash. Distinct first/second delays matter: the source explicitly fixes
a refund-input sequence bug previously hidden by equal delays.
The [BCH/XMR test source](https://github.com/basicswap/basicswap/blob/277b46b0278f1cc76199f7e847988647a1b36e38/tests/basicswap/test_bch_xmr.py)
contains success, reverse-direction, recovery and unequal-delay cases; none were
run during this review.

The [BCH CHECKDATASIG specification](https://upgradespecs.bitcoincashnode.org/op_checkdatasig/)
defines verification over a single SHA-256 of the message, with strict DER and
low-S ECDSA requirements. Monzero's existing Bitcoin transaction-signature APIs
must not silently stand in for this distinct message/encoding contract.

Inference for the Monzero implementation: this is a candidate direct protocol,
not evidence of BCH/XMZ support. Begin with separate BCH contract/data-signature
types, exact fee/destination/delay binding and independent reference vectors.
Native-coin-only support needs an explicit token policy. Subsequent work must bind
fresh per-trade keys and adaptor messages to authenticated terms; connect XMZ
funding/key recovery; preserve private journals and exact-byte relay/reconciliation;
and validate success, both recovery delays, disappearing peers, funding-ID changes,
restart and reorganisation against BCH and XMZ nodes before enabling a market.
These are required parts of the original integration goal, not release claims.

Reference files and their hashes are retained with the existing source-review
manifest, including the upstream license. No reference code was executed, no
BCH production implementation was added, and blockchain fixtures remain stopped.


## 6 October 2026 — BCH data-signature and adaptor primitive

Added `swap-core/src/bch.rs` with `DataMessage`, a separate BCH single-SHA256
message type. It supports encrypted signing, encrypted verification, checked
signature decryption, strict DER/low-S verification and decryption-key recovery.
It never appends or strips a Bitcoin transaction sighash byte. Decryption verifies
the encrypted signature against the message and both keys before releasing the
signature; recovery checks those bindings and the published signature first.

The primitive deliberately supplies no chain, amount, fee or trade binding.
Authenticated fresh per-trade keys, covenant validation and protocol release
conditions must supply them. It constructs no transaction and enables no market.
The initial compile identified a missing prover RNG parameter; this was corrected
to the existing engine's ChaCha20 proof-generation convention before validation.

Two tests passed: a pinned BasicSwap reference DER signature verifies over the
exact destination message, and an adaptor roundtrip recovers the expected key.
They reject changed/double-hashed messages, wrong keys, high-S signatures,
truncated encodings and an appended Bitcoin sighash suffix. The roundtrip result
also verifies independently through libsecp256k1. The reference vector retains
its source link and upstream MIT license under `swap-core/src/bch/`.

`cargo check -p swap-core --all-features --all-targets --release --locked --offline
-j2` passed, as did ordered patch reconstruction. Evidence:
`build/bch-data-signature-tests-20261006.log`,
`build/bch-data-signature-check-20261006.log`, and
`build/bch-data-signature-patch-audit-20261006.log`.
The module and vectors are retained in
`tools/dex-engine-port/upstream-bch-data-signature.patch` and its ordered audit.
Source whitespace was checked; rustfmt remains unavailable.

## 6 October 2026 — BCH covenant bytecode construction

Added `swap-core/src/bch/covenant.rs`, adapting the pinned BasicSwap template
with its copyright notice and retained MIT license. `Covenant::new` constructs
canonical bytecode from explicit absolute fee, redemption/timeout destinations,
compressed signing key and nonzero block delay. Destination support is restricted
to P2PKH, P2SH20 and BCH P2SH32; empty, OP_RETURN and witness programs are rejected.
Fees must be positive and within BCH's monetary range. The private retained terms
cannot be mutated after construction.

The template preserves one-input/one-output constraints, exact fee arithmetic,
CashToken-field preservation, data-signature redemption and CSV timeout forwarding.
`script_pubkey` constructs BCH HASH256 P2SH32; `data_message` binds the redemption
destination using the previous data-signature primitive. `verify_script` compares
all bytecode against the contract built from caller-authenticated terms. It does
not authenticate those terms itself.

and parameter-binding cases. Generated bytecode matches the pinned reference
exactly; its P2SH32 output matches a separately Python-hashed fixture. Each single
byte mutation and an appended opcode are rejected. Fee/destination/key/delay
changes alter the contract, while zero/excessive fees, zero delay and unsupported
destination scripts are rejected. These are construction checks, not a BCH script
interpreter, mining, transaction acceptance or proof of complete recovery.

## 6 October 2026 — BCH native redemption and timeout spend construction

Added `Covenant::prepare_redemption` and `prepare_timeout` in `bch/spend.rs`.
They decode bounded original funding bytes, reject witness/coinbase/null inputs,
require canonical serialization and the exact funding transaction ID, output,
amount and contract, check monetary totals, and apply explicit maximum-fee and
minimum-output policy. CashToken-prefixed outputs are rejected across the funding
transaction, including unrelated outputs, under this native-BCH-only boundary.
The token-prefix handling follows the [CashTokens serialization specification](https://cashtokens.org/docs/spec/chip/#token-encoding);
prefixes are never stripped before transaction identity checks.

Redemption validates its DER data signature and uses sequence zero with the exact
redemption destination. Timeout uses this covenant stage's block delay and exact
timeout destination, without requiring a peer signature. Both construct one-input,
one-output version-2 legacy transactions with zero locktime and exact fee deduction.
Preparation is neither relay authorization nor evidence of consensus validity,
activation, confirmation, unspentness, maturity or completed settlement.

All seven BCH tests passed. New coverage compares redemption bytes to the pinned
reference with only its parent replaced by synthetic funding, exercises two timeout
stages with delays 2/5 and exact successive fee deductions, and rejects incorrect
funding/fee/minimum-output/signature/token/witness/encoding cases on both branches.
No node or script interpreter was used. All swap-core features/targets compile

## 6 October 2026 — BCH two-stage recovery plan

Added `bch::recovery::RecoveryPlan`, which binds both covenant stages and their
amount flow. The initial lock's signed destination is the native funder's BCH
payout, its signing key belongs to the BCH funder, and its timeout destination is
the computed recovery P2SH32 output. The recovery contract uses the native funder's
signing key, refunds the BCH funder through its signed branch, and sends the later
timeout to the native funder's payout. Cancellation and punishment delays remain
separate. Both complete scripts can be checked against the retained plan.

Construction rejects identical participant signing keys, zero delays/fees, invalid
monetary ranges and insufficient funds after both fees and the agreed minimum
output. Spend-term helpers derive amounts/fees for each stage without independent
caller arithmetic. Terms are immutable after construction, but are not yet
network-authenticated or bound to XMZ key proofs.

All ten BCH unit tests passed. New tests follow alternative success, refund and
punishment transactions using synthetic funding; they extract checked redemption
signatures and recover the expected adaptor keys on success and refund. Different
2/5-block delays, exact remaining amounts, minimum-output boundary and substituted
stage rejection are covered. These alternatives do not coexist on a chain, and
no chain acceptance, maturity or actual XMZ recovery is claimed.

## 6 October 2026 — BCH adaptor to XMZ scalar binding

Added `swap-machine/src/bch_key_recovery.rs`. `ProvenNativeAdaptor::verify`
accepts canonical nonidentity torsion-free native public keys only, then verifies
the existing cross-curve DLEQ proof against the BCH adaptor point. The resulting
public binding cannot be constructed by deserializing peer data. It proves a
key relation, not peer identity or authenticated quote ownership.

`recover_share` validates the BCH message/signing/encryption bindings, recovers
the adaptor scalar, converts its byte order using a zeroizing buffer, rejects
native scalar reduction and checks that the result reproduces the proven XMZ
public key. Callers still need the agreed transaction's checked signature,
authenticated terms, local-role policy and current chain confirmation/reorg
handling before using it for a native claim or refund.

secret and combines with the local share into the expected native spend key.

degenerate native keys are rejected. This is an offline cryptographic test,
not XMZ wallet recovery, address ownership, payment or chain settlement.

## 6 October 2026 — BCH shared XMZ wallet key assembly

Added `bch_key_recovery::authenticated::native_wallet`. `NativePair` binds
the ordered, authenticated participant proofs to the quote, rejects reused
adaptor/native keys and rejects a degenerate combined native spend key.
Each private view-share frame is signed by its role's pinned identity for that
exact proof pair. Canonical nonzero view scalars and a nonzero sum are required
before deriving the XMZ address and private view key.
The resulting context includes a commitment to both signed view frames.
View frames contain secrets and require private transport and storage.

`recover_spend_key` verifies the caller's local secret against its authenticated
public share, obtains the other share from the quoted exact BCH success/refund
spend, and verifies that the combined secret reproduces the shared wallet's
public spend key. This is cryptographic key assembly/recovery, not wallet RPC
import, payment, chain confirmation or spending authority.
Local ownership checks before funding, mutual transcript acknowledgement, durable
secret/replay state and both-chain observation/release policy remain required.

All six key-recovery tests passed, including shared-wallet address/view-key
assembly, full spend-key recovery from both success and refund, wrong local
secrets, reused native shares, altered private frames, wrong roles/signatures,
expiry, noncanonical scalars and cancelling view shares.

## 6 October 2026 — BCH cooperative cross-trade input claims

Funding preparation now preflights and retains input claims under the execution
metadata lease before publishing its funding pin. Claim names are scoped by the
quoted BCH network/genesis and outpoint; claim contents bind the trade, quote
and exact preparation digest. All inputs are checked before any claim is written,
so an ordinary conflict on a later input does not claim earlier unrelated inputs.

## 6 October 2026 — retained BCH wallet lock intent and explicit reconciliation

That intent binds admission, preparation, deployment, change address, confirmation policy and original admission time before any `lockunspent(false, ...)` call.
Credentials are excluded from the deployment digest so they can rotate without changing the wallet binding.

## 6 October 2026 — independent BCH signed funding verification

Added `FundingPreview::verify_signed` and immutable `SignedFunding` in swap-core.
The verifier requires every transaction field except input unlocking scripts to match the retained unsigned template exactly.
For each P2PKH input it checks the source public-key hash, two minimal pushes, canonical public-key encoding, strict DER, low S and the ECDSA signature over BCH `SIGHASH_ALL|SIGHASH_FORKID` (0x41).
Other signature modes, witness data, trailing bytes and changed input/output fields are rejected.
CashTokens remain unsupported; non-P2PKH source scripts accepted by the unsigned preview are explicitly rejected by this signature verifier pending separate implementations.

The BCH signature-hash preimage was checked against pinned BCHN v29.0.0 source and four upstream ALL|FORKID test vectors, including their nonzero high fork-id bits.
Production verification requires exactly 0x41.
The signed transaction exposes its final legacy funding outpoint and exact verified transaction; the unsigned template ID must never be used for recovery messages.
Different valid signer-generated signatures can still change a legacy transaction ID, so a future signing executor must retain the exact signed bytes before publishing recovery messages.

## 6 October 2026 — exact BCH funding observation for relay reconciliation

Added read-only `BchRpc::observe_funding` and admitted-execution `observe_signed_bch_funding`.
The executor restores the exact signed transaction and checks the independently retained wallet/deployment binding before observation, including for historical recovery after quote expiry.
The backend checks owned deployment/chain/wallet identity, queries the exact contract outpoint with mempool spends included, and compares its script and exact amount to the saved transaction.
Wrong tip, coinbase/token-bearing output data, negative/malformed confirmations or counts beyond the reported chain height are rejected.

The result distinguishes confirmed unspent funding, funding present in the mempool with an unspent contract output, funding in the mempool whose contract output is already spent, and unobserved funding.
Mempool entry size must match the saved legacy transaction, whose txid binds its exact bytes.
The RPC transport accepts absence only for getmempoolentry's explicit -5 error with null result and a matching request ID; authentication failures, transport errors, other RPC errors and malformed envelopes remain errors.
The chain tip and wallet are rechecked before returning.
Mempool state may still change without a tip change, so this is a point-in-time owned-node observation, not an SPV proof, payment/release decision or relay permit.

Unobserved includes unknown, evicted, conflicting or already-spent confirmed funding.
It never proves that funding was not broadcast, and this change does not implement automatic resubmission or a broadcast method.

### Litecoin light-wallet proof boundary — implementation, validation pending

Added `swap-machine/src/litecoin_light.rs` as an offline foundation for the approved light-wallet path.
`script_hash` computes the Electrum reversed SHA256 script identifier.
`match_merkle_proof` bounds the transaction, 80-byte header and JSON response before parsing;
it matches caller-selected request ID, transaction ID, block hash and claimed height,
checks branch order/endianness/root and rejects unconsumed position bits,
ambiguous 64-byte non-witness leaves, malformed envelopes and excessive depth.
The initial wire contract requires JSON-RPC 2.0 and the Electrum 1.4 Merkle-result shape.

`MerkleMatch` is a non-serializable mathematical match, not chain or spendability authority.
No Litecoin Scrypt work, difficulty, active-chain membership, header height, confirmations,
witness validity, current unspentness or MWEB acceptance is established here.
The module cannot produce `VerifiedLiveLock` and is not connected to any signing or funding gate.
The seven tests use independently generated Python hashlib vectors and explicitly test witness limitations.
No external wallet server is contacted.
Ordered patch reconstruction passed; compile/runtime validation is in progress.

Implementation still required: authenticated transport and protocol/network negotiation;
Litecoin header validation and persistent chain selection/reorganisation handling;
transaction history and spend discovery without confusing omission with proof of unspentness;
local wallet creation/restoration, ownership, signing and reservations;
then receive/balance UI and complete swap/recovery acceptance through the new backend.
The existing Core RPC path remains the only execution backend.

Protocol references: [ElectrumX Merkle methods](https://electrumx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/protocol-methods.html#blockchain-transaction-get-merkle),
[ElectrumX script hashing](https://electrumx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/protocol-basics.html),
and [Litecoin header identity versus Scrypt work](https://github.com/litecoin-project/litecoin/blob/master/src/primitives/block.cpp).

### Litecoin light-wallet read session — implementation, validation pending

Added `litecoin_light::session::ReadSession` over a caller-supplied asynchronous stream.
It negotiates exactly Electrum 1.4 and checks the reported genesis against the selected
Litecoin mainnet/testnet/regtest identity and script hashing against SHA256 before transaction queries.
This checks the server's claim, not its honesty or chain consensus.
Production callers still need to construct and authenticate a TLS connection.

The read-only inclusion path requests the specified header, exact transaction and Merkle branch,
then uses the existing offline checker against caller-selected block identity and height.
It never discovers a trusted chain anchor from the same response.
There are no wallet keys, signing, subscriptions, automatic retries or broadcast methods.

Each request has an identity, a bounded newline-delimited response and a whole-request deadline.
Malformed/error responses, wrong headers and proof failures invalidate the session.
The session becomes unusable before the first request await, so cancelling a pending future
also prevents a late response from being reused by the next request.
Six added duplex-stream fixtures cover fragmented complete proof retrieval, request order and parameters,
wrong chain/hash algorithm, unsupported protocol, wrong/duplicate IDs and server errors,
wrong-header refusal without further queries, EOF/oversized lines and timeout/cancellation.
No external server or real node is contacted.
Ordered reconstruction passed for `upstream-litecoin-light-session.patch`; runtime and compile checks are pending.

### Litecoin durable address allocation — implementation, 10 October 2026

`AddressBook` binds its private journal to the full account public key/chain code,
master fingerprint, account index and network genesis through a domain-separated digest.
Creation is explicit; reopening requires an existing valid record and cannot silently reset it.
A non-nil request UUID identifies each allocation. Repeating it returns the same branch/index;
reusing it for another branch fails. Receive/change indices advance independently.
The complete bounded record is compared and atomically replaced under the existing directory
lease before an address is returned. Publication errors invalidate the handle until reopen,
including an injected lost result after a successful durable replacement. Out-of-lease changes
are rejected and invalidate the handle. No private keys are written.
The journal primitive adds a bounded compare-and-replace method; existing execution-head behavior
is unchanged. Tests cover retry/restart, branch separation, lease exclusion, account/seed/network
mismatch, malformed state, changed records, pre-publication failure and uncertain publication.

### Litecoin bounded address discovery — 10 October 2026

`ReadSession::scan_branch` derives and queries one BIP84 account branch from index zero.
The account network must match the negotiated session before any query.
The caller supplies the known allocated count; `AddressBook::allocated_count` exposes that count after checking the retained journal.
A reported gap is counted only beyond the allocated range, and any nonempty history resets it.
The caller explicitly chooses a gap of 1..1,000, an address budget of 1..10,000 and a total history-entry budget of 1..10,000.
Results distinguish `ReportedGap` from `AddressBudget`, retaining nonempty address histories with their indices.

### Litecoin observed-set accounting — 10 October 2026

`ObservedWallet::reconcile` recomputes wallet-script receipts minus spends in an explicitly supplied included-transaction set.

### Litecoin encrypted seed vault foundation — 10 October 2026

`SecretSeed` owns 32 bytes in a zeroizing, non-Debug/non-Clone/non-serializable type, with explicit OS-entropy generation or caller-owned restoration.
It derives public BIP84 accounts without exposing a public private-key serializer.
`SeedVault` stores a fixed-size 176-byte authenticated record under the existing private directory lease and atomic publication rules.
The versioned format uses Scrypt N=2^17, r=8, p=1 (128 MiB) and XChaCha20-Poly1305 from pinned RustCrypto 0.10.1.
The dependency already existed in the lockfile; this adds its direct use without changing its version.
Fresh 16-byte salt and 24-byte nonce come from the OS RNG on creation.
Version, network genesis, wallet UUID, salt and nonce are authenticated associated data.
Opening requires exact record length/version/network/wallet identity, and synchronizes recovered state before unlock.
Wrong password or ciphertext/header tampering fails; creation cannot replace an existing vault, and changed-on-disk records cannot be unlocked through an old handle.
Passwords are exact nonempty byte strings up to 1,024 bytes; password strength/UX policy is not implemented here.
The implementation uses in-place encryption/decryption and zeroizes owned plaintext and derived-key buffers.
This is not an mlock/secure-memory guarantee: dependency internals may copy secrets, and swap/core-dump hardening remains outstanding.
The caller retains responsibility for seed backup and any password/entropy copies.
Independent Python Scrypt/libsodium PUBLIC TEST vectors reproduce exact ciphertext; tests also cover restart, context mismatch, tampering, randomized encryption and password limits.
Reference: https://docs.rs/chacha20poly1305/0.10.1/chacha20poly1305/

### Litecoin encrypted vault lifecycle — 10 October 2026

Changing a password does not revoke old backups, which still decrypt with the old password.

### 2026-10-11 — bounded Litecoin fee reporting and size estimates verified

`ReadSession::reported_fee_rate` adds the Electrum 1.4 `blockchain.estimatefee` request with explicit target and atomic-rate ceiling.
It preserves unavailable estimates as `None`, rejects malformed/negative/excessive rates, and poisons the session on remote failure while leaving locally invalid requests without I/O.
Original decimal/exponent spellings are converted with integer arithmetic, rounding fractional atomic rates upward.
`ReportedFeeRate::p2wpkh_fee` estimates an upper-bound virtual size using 73-byte signature and 33-byte key witnesses, rounds the absolute fee upward, and enforces a caller maximum.
It assumes all inputs are native P2WPKH; it does not establish ownership, relay policy, freshness, or confirmation guarantees.

### 2026-10-11 — Litecoin payment inclusion and reorganization reconciliation

`ClaimedSpend::observe_payment_on` verifies retained signatures and queries only the original payment script's bounded history.
It fetches and compares the exact signed bytes for a matching report, then validates a Merkle branch against the selected Scrypt-validated header when the server reports a block position.
The result distinguishes NotReported, ReportedPending and Included, retaining selected height/tip and inclusion depth.
An observation cannot be reused through its typed accessor after the selected chain changes.
A missing report is not proof of rejection, pending membership is only a peer report, and header inclusion does not claim full transaction/UTXO consensus validation or global-chain freshness.
No observation signs, sends or releases input claims.

The helper adds `--wallet-reconcile-stdio-v1`, requiring the original payment/review and operation, explicit maximumDownloadHeaders (1..10,000,000) and maximumHistoryEntries (1..1,000).
This explicit chain-check operation first synchronizes the header cache and requires the reported tip to match the selected tip, then observes the retained payment without a vault.
It rejects signing/send approval and wallet-scan fields.
The receipt carries separate local broadcast status and confirmationStatus=not-reported, reported-pending or included.
`paymentObservation` records selectedHeight, selectedTip, height/blockHash (null when not included), confirmations and observedAtUnix.
The helper does not persist a proof as permanent confirmation; each chain check recomputes it, while offline send-status inspection remains confirmation-unassessed.

### 2026-10-11 — Offline Litecoin encrypted backup helper

The helper now accepts explicit wallet-backup-save and wallet-backup-verify operations.
Each request uses its matching monzero-ltc-light-<mode>-request-v1 schema, a nonnil requestId,
and backupApproval containing an absolute canonical private directory and password.
Passwords use the existing bounded, zeroizing stdin transport; request size is limited to 8192 bytes.
Signing, broadcast, payment, quote, retained-review, scan and header/history-budget fields are forbidden.
Other helper modes reject backupApproval.
No network connection or header-cache access is required.

Save opens the configured address book and vault, authenticates their account binding, exports the existing encrypted seed/allocation bundle,
then publishes litecoin-wallet.backup through private durable storage with authenticated read-back.
A new export never overwrites different existing ciphertext; use a new directory for a new backup generation.
If output is lost after saving, explicitly verify the existing destination.
Verify authenticates the saved bundle against configured network, wallet identity and public account without requiring live vault/address-book files.
Neither operation restores a wallet, signs, sends or enables trading.

Responses contain schema, requestId, executable=false and wallet.
The wallet object has watchOnly=true, spendable=false, backupVerified=true, backupSaved, backupDigest,
walletId, receivingAllocated, changeAllocated, scope=seed-and-address-allocations,
allocationFreshness=unassessed and activeSwapRecovery=false.
No seed, password, account xpub or bundle bytes appear in stdout.
Allocation counts describe the saved snapshot; verification does not establish freshness, an independent/offline copy,
or recovery of payment claims, signed transactions or active swap state.

### 2026-10-11 — Durable new Litecoin wallet setup library

vault::setup::initialize now provides the storage foundation for explicit new-wallet creation.
It accepts a setup directory, distinct vault/address/backup directories, selected network, wallet UUID,
hardened account index and bounded password. All directories must already be canonical, private and owned.

Before publishing a vault, setup durably retains litecoin-wallet-setup.json containing fixed context and an encrypted generated seed.
No plaintext seed or password is serialized. The intent is an additional encrypted seed copy; password changes cannot revoke it or older backups.
A retry authenticates and reuses this exact encrypted seed. Changed identity, network, index or paths are rejected.
Fresh setup refuses to adopt existing vault, address or backup records.
The setup directory holds its process lease through the operation.

Setup publishes the encrypted vault and identical empty address book, then saves and authenticates the initial encrypted backup.
If that backup was already published before an interruption, it authenticates and reuses the existing backup rather than generating a replacement.
Account identity and empty allocation counts must match. Only then is litecoin-wallet-ready.json retained and a CreatedWallet returned,
containing public account and authenticated backup information.
Errors may leave partial records; identical retries complete publication without replacing different records or keys.
Repeating setup after later address allocations fails without resetting those allocations.
This API does not activate the wallet, connect to peers, sign, send or enable trading, and it does not claim an independent/offline backup copy.

## Private app process channel — 11 October 2026

Implemented a Linux-only blocking channel intended for a background worker.
It checks the installed executable and the digest of its execution descriptor,
uses bounded local sockets rather than public JSON/status buffers, and erases
requests and raw replies on every outcome.
Only a clean child exit plus strict operation/request/trade response validation
can populate private signing material.
Timeout, cancellation, stderr, excess output and malformed replies fail closed.
The owned process group is terminated and its child reaped on cleanup.

## Shared light wallet for Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash and Dogecoin — 12 October 2026

The Litecoin light wallet (`swap-machine/src/litecoin_light`) is now a shared
UTXO light-wallet core. A runtime `LightNetwork` names both chain and
deployment (`Litecoin`, `Bitcoin`, `BitcoinCash`, `Dogecoin`), so the existing
runtime network checks also keep chains apart. Litecoin behaviour, persisted
formats, schema strings and error messages are unchanged: every public function
still accepts `LtcNetwork`, and all 153 original light-wallet tests pass by name.

- `network.rs`: chain identity, genesis headers, header consensus per chain
  (Litecoin rules moved verbatim; Bitcoin per Bitcoin Core, including the
  testnet3 minimum-difficulty rule and BIP34/65/66 heights), SLIP-44 coin types,
  BIP84/BIP44 purposes, `SegwitAddress` (byte-identical to `LtcSegwitAddress`
  for Litecoin), CashAddr and Base58Check `LegacyAddress`, and a per-chain
  `storage_identity` (the genesis for Litecoin/Bitcoin/Dogecoin, a tagged hash
  for Bitcoin Cash, whose genesis is Bitcoin's).
- `script.rs`: P2WPKH (BIP84), P2PKH with the legacy signature hash (Dogecoin)
  and P2PKH with the BIP143 SIGHASH_FORKID hash (Bitcoin Cash); signature
  placement and read-back verification; maximum-size fee templates. The BIP143
  implementation reproduces rust-bitcoin's independent P2WPKH digest.
- Signing, reload verification, fee estimation and the helper use the script
  kind. P2PKH signatures are part of the txid, so the helper now checks that only
  spending data changed and takes the final txid from the retained signed bytes.
- The helper selects the chain from the request schema tag (`ltc`, `btc`, `bch`,
  `doge`); configuration, setup and response schemas carry the same tag.
- Bitcoin Cash and Dogecoin mainnet/testnet header validation is refused with an
  explicit error until a post-fork checkpoint with ASERT (Bitcoin Cash) and
  DigiShield, AuxPoW and checkpoints (Dogecoin) are implemented. Only their
  regtest rules are enabled.

Validation (all regtest, isolated nodes, disposable keys):

- Unit: 176 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored (153 original unchanged, 23 new network
  and script tests with real Bitcoin mainnet headers including the block 32256
  retarget, BIP173/BIP84/CashAddr specification vectors and BCHN/Dogecoin node
  address vectors). [Log](../build/light-wallet-unit-tests-20261012.log).
- End to end with `test_light_wallet_chain.py` (create encrypted wallet, receive
  a real payment, refresh, prepare, sign, broadcast, confirm, reconcile, refresh)
  against Bitcoin Core 31.1.0, Bitcoin Cash Node 29.0.0 and Dogecoin 1.14.9 through
  a local TLS Electrum peer computed from the node. Each node accepted the
  signatures with its own interpreter; Bitcoin Core also derived the receive
  address independently. [BTC](../build/light-wallet-btc-20261012.json),
  [BCH](../build/light-wallet-bch-20261012.json),
  [DOGE](../build/light-wallet-doge-20261012.json).
- The existing actual-node Litecoin fixture (`test_litecoin_light_chain.py
  --create-wallet --reconcile`) passed with the new helper:
  [LTC regression](../build/light-wallet-ltc-regression-20261012.json).
- Patch `upstream-light-network-core.patch` (31 files) reconstructs the engine

## 2026-10-15 — exact success publication repair; runtime pending

Success publication now retains an exact private candidate before writing the
public pin and final private record. A partial candidate is not regenerated or
exposed automatically. Separate node/local repair review and execution APIs
validate the retained source, admission, proof, frame and original timestamp,
then finish only the exact approved candidate. Repair returns no frame and no
chain approval. Signed repair requires published preparation; prepared repair
checks deterministic agreed bytes and every available signed copy's pairing.

private record without a trusted pin is rejected as metadata loss/rollback,
not silently reanchored. Conflicting pins/private bytes/candidates fail closed.
Legacy complete records without candidates remain readable and gain candidates
on a fresh checked release. Missing legacy private bytes without a candidate
cannot be synthesized from their public hash.

## 15 October 2026 — owned-service desktop refund-wallet submission worker

BchRefundWalletJob::submit now requires a live current review, exact commitment,

### 2026-10-15 — BCH recovery-wallet controller ownership
The native DEX controller now attaches only the configured live app-owned recovery
service and accepts a submission only with a fresh matching approval and an available
durable operation token. Failed/lost replies remain recovery-required, with no automatic
retry. Password buffers are consumed on rejected controller submissions as well.
Owner availability notifications are queued to prevent reentrant operations. Controller
teardown disconnects the owner before destroying child jobs. Claude reviewed this wiring;
disposition: build/claude-bch-refund-wallet-owned-controller-disposition-20261015.txt.

### 2026-10-15 — BCH recovery-wallet startup coordinator (Claude)
New hidden option --dex-bch-refund-wallet-service <config> (requires --dex-bch-refund-wallet,
conflicts with --dex-bch-refund-wallet-review). Canonical private config schema
monzero-private-bch-refund-wallet-service-v1, exactly: tradeId (must equal the status trade),
program, programSha256, directory, daemonPort, walletPort, bchRpcFile, observerRpcFile.
DexEngine::configureBchRefundWalletService creates only the bound directory itself (0700,
never parents), starts SwapWalletRpcProcess::startBoundWithDigest, then retries
provisionBchRefundWalletService every 250 ms (max 60 s) after processStarted. Status gains
serviceState: unconfigured/starting/attached/start-refused/attach-failed/stopped/recovery-required.
A refused start (binding mismatch, recovery-required, operation-pending, active, foreign files)
leaves files untouched and never falls back to a fresh service. Attach timeout stops cleanly
so the next start can resume. aboutToQuit runs a bounded blocking clean stop (15 s).
Dex.qml shows the service state. Not verified: real monzero-wallet-rpc SIGTERM exit code
(fixture treats SIGTERM as unclean, so shutdown is only checked to terminate and record state).
